Stevenage vs Reading

Cambridge vs Millwall

Birmingham vs Brentford

Southampton vs West Ham

Watford vs Peterborough

Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon

Plymouth/Exeter vs Coventry

Chelsea vs Luton

Tottenham vs Charlton

Several matches even featured hydration breaks in a controversial decision to many fans.

Another new rule introduced this season will see substitutes wait to come onto the pitch if the player they are replacing takes too long to leave the field.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish told fans would love perfect transfer to Premier League club
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor has insisted the majority of Aston Villa fans would welcome Jack Grealish back at the club.

The 30-year-old is facing an uncertain future, having returned to Manchester City this summer after Everton opted not to take up the £50million buy option in his loan deal.

4 Grealish grew up as a Villa fan and came through the ranks at the club to captain them Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Having fallen out of favour at the Etihad Stadium before moving to the Toffees, it is currently unclear whether Grealish will be given a chance to prove himself under new boss Enzo Maresca.

This has fed speculation that the Englishman could leave permanently this summer, with City keen on selling him as he is entering the final year of his contract.

While talkSPORT understands Grealish is drawing interest from Saudi side Al Hilal, he would prefer to stay in the Premier League.

Another potential next destination which has been mooted is former club Aston Villa, five years on from his £100million exit.

Grealish joined the Citizens from boyhood club Villa in 2021 for a then British record transfer, having established himself as a cult hero during his time at the club.

After rising through the youth ranks at Villa Park, the forward went on to become captain, leading his team back to the Premier League in 2019 after a three-year absence, before starring for them in next two years in the top flight.

A move could also be advantageous for Villa, who are keen to strengthen their forward line after losing star man Morgan Rogers to Chelsea in a new British record £117m move.

Happy homecoming?

While Grealish left Villa fans heartbroken when he left for City five years ago, talkSPORT host and club icon Agbonlahor has insisted he would be welcomed back with open arms should he choose to return.

Agbonlahor said: "I would love him to come back, but it's a question for if Jack wants to come back, it's a question if the manager wants Jack.

“I think he'd love to come back to Villa, yeah. He's a Villa fan. He loves Aston Villa. I would have him back tomorrow.

4 Grealish may find himself further down the pecking order at City after returning from Everton Credit: Getty

4 Grealish captained Aston Villa to victory in the Championship Play-Off Final in 2019, sealing the club's return to the Premier League Credit: Getty - Contributor

Despite tipping Grealish for a homecoming, Agbonlahor admitted Villa boss Unai Emery may have different plans for his team, pointing to the recent loan signing of Alejandro Garnacho.

He continued: "But has the manager got other ideas for that left-hand side? We are short in that position, 100 per cent.

“I'd take Jack over Garnacho any day. All day, every day of the week.”

Continuing to state a case for Grealish to return, Agbonlahor insisted that he left Villa on good enough terms to be welcomed back.

That is despite the England international being booed by his old fans on his return to Villa Park with Man City in 2021.

On Grealish's 2021 exit, Agbonlahor continued: “It was no problem. There was a release clause in the contract that he left. I think the majority of them would [take him back], yeah.

4 Grealish could be given a chance to impress new Man City boss Enzo Maresca Credit: Getty

“I reckon 90-95 per cent of Villa fans would say yes. If he's going to make our team better, he's a Villa fan. And let's not forget, he didn't leave in a bad situation. He got the club £100million.

“They used that money elsewhere. Exactly. So I think it would be an amazing signing.

“Just down to the manager, if he wants him, it'll be interesting.”

Despite this, Agbonlahor admitted it remains a possibility that Grealish could yet stay at Man City, if he is given a second chance under new boss Maresca.

He added: “I think there's a chance that he does stay at Man City as well. Because he knows Maresca, Maresca was a coach under Pep [Guardiola] as well. So he knows him. He could stay, yeah.”

Sports.title: Why Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor – and it’s not just about the 50 per cent wage rise
Sports.content:
Why Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor – and it’s not just about the 50 per cent wage rise

Mohamed Salah had plenty more reasons to join Trabzonspor rather than just a bumper pay rise, says talkSPORT's Andy Brassell.

Salah completed a free transfer to the Turkish club last Tuesday, penning a two-year deal.



3 Trabzonspor is the seventh different club Salah has played for Credit: AFP

It is an impressively lucrative move for Salah as he will receive a monster salary of £14.5million a season.

Salah stands to rake in even more funds as he will earn a 20 per cent share of products sold in his name along with conditional bonuses.

Despite the dizzying deal, European football expert Brassell believes there was far more to Salah's decision-making process ahead of joining Trabzonspor.



Andy Brassell explains why Mohamed Salah joined Trabzonspor

"Clearly, he could have made more in Saudi Arabia," Brassell said on talkSORT's Trans Euro Express.

"But clearly, he never really seemed to show any inclination to go out there. And for them to be able to sign an Arab superstar, for the Saudi Pro League it would have been absolutely huge. I suspect that's part of it as well.



"Nicolas Anelka spoke in the past about when he went to Fenerbahce, a huge part of it was at that point in his life, he wanted to live and play in a Muslim country. I suspect that's at least part of it for Mo Salah as well.

"But for so many players, and we're seeing prime age players, players younger than Mo Salah going to big Turkish Super Lig clubs. It's the fact that you can get paid better than you can in western Europe without having to leave the competitiveness of European football and UEFA club competitions, I think that's really key as well."



This summer has proven especially eye-catching when it comes to younger players moving to big Turkish clubs.

One example is former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood, who joined Fenerbahce from Marseille for approximately £38m at just 24 years of age.

Fenerbahce have also snapped up centre-back Nathan Ake while Galatasaray are targeting Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli, who is 25 years old.

3 Despite being 34 years old, Salah is keen to prove he still has what it takes to compete Credit: Getty



No matter their age, all will be vying for the Turkish Super Lig title.

It is a trophy Galatasaray have had a vice-like grip on, having won four consecutive league crowns.

How Mohamed Salah is hoping to inspire Trabzonspor to former glories

Prior to Galatasaray's run, the last team to have had the league title in their possession was Trabzonspor, who accomplished the feat in 2021/22.

Aside from their recent success, Trabzonspor boasts a fan base unlike any other, something which Salah has already experienced as thousands turned out to welcome him at the airport and even more attended his unveiling at their stadium.



"They're passionately supported out there on the Black Sea in a city that leaves and breathes football, which must be part of it as well," Brassell continued.

"I think even for experienced players, the minute you get off the plane and see all the fans, it's a pinch-me moment.

3 Salah received a hero's welcome at Papara Park Credit: Getty

"You get to play in busy stadiums that are so, so passionate in a level that even coming from the Premier League, you just can't understand. That is a huge part of it."



It's not just the Turkish Super Lig that Salah and his new teammates will be eyeing off.

Thanks to their third-place finish last term, Trabzonspor qualified for the Europa League play-off round and will face either Hungarian side Ferencvaros or Polish outfit Gornik Zabrze.

Galatasaray was the first and remains the only Turkish club to have won the competition, doing so in 2000.

But the marquee signing of Salah, who scored over 250 goals for Liverpool, could be the perfect tonic to help Trabzonspor win their first European trophy in history.

Sports.title: Barcelona set to avoid extra payment to Man City as Ferran Torres closes in on £42m transfer
Sports.content:
Barcelona set to avoid extra payment to Man City as Ferran Torres closes in on £42m transfer

Barcelona are set to avoid paying an add-on fee to Manchester City as he closes in on a £42million move to Paris Saint-Germain.

Torres joined Barcelona from Man City back in January 2022 for an initial €55million, signing a contract until the summer of 2027.



2 Torres is out of contract at the Camp Nou next summer Credit: Getty

But the versatile forward has emerged as an option for the back-to-back Champions League winners.

Should the deal be completed, it might also open up a potential departure for Bradley Barcola, with Liverpool very keen.

The cost of keeping Torres

Barcelona have already paid Man City €10m in add-ons, but they’ll have to pay around a further €8m if the Spain international extends his contract at the Camp Nou, The Athletic report.



As such, LaLiga champions Barca are said to be erring against offering Torres a new contract.

And with the 26-year-old not becoming a free agent until next summer, he would command a fee in the current transfer window.



Torres scored the winner in the World Cup final for Spain as he slammed home late on to ensure La Roja beat Argentina at the MetLife Stadium.

It made Spain two-time world champions and ensured Torres' name is in history forever.



The former Valencia man made 49 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions last season, scoring a career-best 21 goals.

That being said, he endured a 14-game goal drought between January and April and lost the starting place he’d gained from Robert Lewandowski.

With that in mind, Barcelona may not be overly concerned about parting ways with him this summer.

Torres has found the net 65 times in his four-and-a-half years at Barcelona, winning three LaLiga titles and a Copa del Rey.



He previously won the Premier League title and EFL Cup in his only full campaign at Man City, as well as reaching the Champions League final.

2 Torres joined Andreas Iniesta in becoming just the second man to score for Spain in a World Cup final

Spain's super-sub

As far as goalscoring goes, he’s fared better in international football, striking 25 times in 65 caps since making his senior Spain debut six years ago.

Part of the squad that went all the way at Euro 2024, Torres mostly featured as a substitute at the 2026 World Cup, and he came off the bench again to win the World Cup for his country.



A changing of the guard

Barcelona have already offloaded two players for fees this off-season, with goalkeeper Inaki Pena and attacking midfielder Ansu Fati joining Panathinaikos and Monaco respectively.

Meanwhile, veteran striker Lewandowski has left following the expiry of his contract, joining MLS side Chicago Fire.

In terms of inbound business, Anthony Gordon has been the sole signing so far, joining for £70m.

Arriving from Newcastle, the England star became only the third English player to sign for Barcelona since the Second World War.



Gordon's international teammate Marcus Rashford spent last season on loan at the Camp Nou, but his move has not been made permanent, with Barcelona signing Karim Adeyemi.

Sports.title: Endrick told why he should reject Aston Villa to sign for European giant
Sports.content:
Endrick told why he should reject Aston Villa to sign for European giant

Endrick has been told to turn down a loan move to Aston Villa in favour of joining Roma.

talkSPORT understands the Villans are considering bringing the Real Madrid starlet to Villa Park on loan, having found playing time hard to come by since moving Spain in 2024.

4 Endrick could make his first step in English football this summer Credit: Getty

Endrick spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon from the Spanish giants, and has since returned to the club this summer.

The 20-year-old scored eight goals and added eight assists in 21 appearances for Lyon during his loan spell.

But he could seal another temporary switch away from the Santiago Bernabeu this summer, with the recent arrival of Yan Diomande likely to push Endrick further down the pecking order.

Villa, who are looking to bolster their attacking options as they prepare for Champions League football in the upcoming season, are among the clubs considering offering him a shot at regular game time.

Unai Emery's side have already had to deal with some high-profile departures - namely Morgan Rogers' British record transfer to Chelsea and Youri Tielemans leaving to join Manchester United.

But Villa aren't the only side keen on Endrick, with Serie A side Roma also interested in snapping him up on a short-term basis.

The bigger picture

While a loan move to Aston Villa would give Endrick an opportunity to prove himself in the Premier League, European football expert Andy Brassell believes this may not be best for his development.

He insisted that the physicality of the Premier League wouldn't best prepare the Brazilian for a long-term career at Real Madrid, claiming a move to Italy with Roma could benefit him more.

Asked if a move to Villa could be a possibility, he told talkSPORT: “It could be, it shouldn't be. I'm not sure it's in his best interests at this point in time.

"Of course he was loaned to Lyon in Ligue 1 for the second half of last season. And he did pretty well. I think it's easy to look at it from a distance and say he did really well. Pretty well is the truth. He had some really good bits, he had some difficult bits."

4 Emery will need squad depth this season as Villa look to compete in Europe Credit: Getty

4 Endrick's strong run of form for Lyon saw him named in Brazil's World Cup squad Credit: Getty

Brassell continued: "He's got everything to be a superstar.

“In terms of what you can do on the pitch, it's not there yet. I think ideally he probably would have gone back to Lyon for a year - that would have been good for him.

“Real Madrid obviously wanted [Jose] Mourinho to have a look at him. And now because of the signing of Diomande and many other forward options that they've got, they've got to clear the decks. And they will loan Endrick out, it looks like.

"I think of the options out there, Roma is the one that makes the most sense. They're looking for wired players.

"Serie A is a subtle step up from where he was in the second half of last season. He can continue to progress and he'll play loads.

“I just think if he goes to Villa, it's not really training him for LaLiga. He'll get kicked loads and he probably won't play every game."

4 There were high hopes for Endrick when Real Madrid agreed to sign him as a 16-year-old in 2022 Credit: Rex

Options

While Brassell felt a loan to Aston Villa could hinder Endrick's long-term future at Real Madrid, he admitted the Brazilian could put himself in the shop window for a permanent move next summer by impressing on loan in the Premier League.

On a potential loan move to Villa, he added: "I don't really see what the benefit is for Real Madrid there, unless they're now moving towards selling him. Because I think what would be the smart thing.

“If they're looking to selling him, of course the most lucrative market is the Premier League.

"So you put him out there, if he looks like the business in the Premier League, don't attach a buy option for Villa. Then you can sell him for what you want at the end of the season.

“But of course they might need an obligation, they might need money in the short term, because they've been out there spending a lot of money. Certainly in terms of contracts, they'll be spending loads more.

“I just hope he gets somewhere where he's going to play and be an important player.”

Sports.title: James McClean's dream return to hometown club turns into a nightmare: Derry City attempt to rip up poppy-protest footballer's contract - with defiant star, 37, set for training ground showdown
Sports.content:
James McClean's homecoming story looks to have taken a sour turn after his club informed the 37-year-old that they intended to rip up his contract due to a perceived lack of 'physical capacity' required to fulfil its terms.

McClean, who has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations, signed for his hometown club Derry City at the start of the 2026 season.

But, according to the Irish Independent, the club have told McClean they are ending his contract despite it still having two years left to run, claiming he is unable to fulfil its terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

The report states that McClean disputes that assessment and is keen to continue playing, with the former Wrexham full back still set to report for training this week.

McClean, who has started just 12 of sixth-placed Derry City's 27 league games this season, is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally and that an independent physician is required to determine his fitness, the report states.

It has been a turbulent few weeks for McClean, who has regularly taken to social media to criticise his side. He also posted a picture showing he was watching former side Wrexham play a Carabao Cup match at the same time Derry City were playing a home league game.

McClean, who has started just 12 of sixth-placed Derry City's 27 league games this season, is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

In June, the 37-year-old hinted at his unhappiness following his return home after a 15-year spell in English football.

'Family (are) enjoying being home – probably not so much myself, if I’m being honest,' McClean said during a punditry appearance on RTE.

'You know, you have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and you quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

'There’s a lot of factors that’s contributed to that, but we’ll leave them for another day.'

McClean has previously spoken out about his reasons for not wearing the poppy, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012. He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean said in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour world war 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both world wars.

McClean, who has won more than 100 caps for Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he had received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won more than 100 caps for Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy," and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

Sports.title: There's a new Team GB sprint Queen! Amy Hunt dethrones Dina Asher-Smith and storms to 100m European gold - and there could be more to come
Sports.content:
There's a new Team GB sprint Queen! Amy Hunt dethrones Dina Asher-Smith and storms to 100m European gold - and there could be more to come

Sprint sensation Amy Hunt continued her sizzling summer by storming to a landmark European gold in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old clocked 11.00s to land her first major individual triumph and dethrone reigning champion Dina Asher-Smith, who finished fifth.

'I was getting fed up of silver,' said Hunt, who finished second in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow. 'It is so special to do this at home.

'I had such a big premonition, and I just love my job. This is what makes it the best.

'I just had such a magical feeling. I've won English Schools here, I've raced here as a kind of 13, 14-year-old, so, this is really my track. I'm a girl, I'm from Newark, so I just had a feeling that this was going to be my night.

'My first gold. I think it was definitely time for an upgrade. I think this was definitely a coming of age for me here tonight, and I'm now kind of fully established.

'I'm a 100m medallist, I've got two 100m medals in the last two weeks, and one more sub-11 to boot. I'm very, very happy.'

Hunt narrowly held off Poland's Eva Swoboda, who finished two-hundredths of a second behind, with Belgium's Delphine Nkansa earning bronze.

Amy Hunt is the new European champion after taking gold in the 100m sprint

Grantham rocket Amy Hunt will be competing across four fronts in Birmingham this week

It is the start of what she hopes will be a historic week as she targets gold on four fronts, with the 200m - in which she won World Championship silver last year - and a pair of relays to come.

'I want to be the best. I don't shy away from that. I train incredibly hard, and I back myself so incredibly hard. I'm not saying that I'm the best right now, but that's something I aspire to be.'

Hunt set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 10.99s to ease into the showpiece.

Reigning champion Asher-Smith also made it through but could only play a bit part in the final on this occasion in the latest sign of a shift in the balance of power within British sprinting.

'The stage of a final doesn’t intimidate me and I just knew I had to stay calm and not overthink myself into the goal,' Hunt said.

'That was why the Commonwealths really came in handy for me. That’s why I really wanted to do it, to have that experience of being in front of a home crowd, having that medal expectation, because I've never had that before.'

Hunt credited the unlikely trio of Megan Thee Stallion, High School Musical and Mamma Mia as key to keeping her calm in the build-up, along with keeping her brain active on Wordle.

As in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow, her start left her with catching up to do but she never had cause to press the panic button.

'One of my biggest skills in terms of championships is I know I'm so strong in the end and I always have that kind of extra magic in the last 40,' she said.

'It can definitely rescue me in situations that I've got myself into but I kind of know the distance I can be away from the girls in order to be able to come back.

'I did leave it a little bit last minute this time but in championships, it's all about crossing the line first.

'When I look back at this race in 10 years, I'm not going to think about how far back I was after 30 metres.'

Hunt returns to action on Wednesday in her ‘favourite event’, the 200m. Her plans before that are refreshingly simple.

'Try to get as much sleep as possible and a big fat lie-in.' After this, she has earned it.

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan with an option to buy.

The 27-year-old defender flew to Merseyside on Sunday afternoon and has since completed his medical.

The Reds have the option to purchase the Uruguay international at the end of the campaign for £47million.

'I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy,' Araujo said.

'I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my teammates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

'I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

'As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time.'

Liverpool have confirmed the loan signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo

The Uruguayan defender has joined the Anfield club on a season long loan

Araujo added that he will take inspiration from 'role model' Virgil van Dijk when he lines up alongside the Liverpool captain.

'We all know what a great player Virgil is. He's a real reference point for the team and he's a kind of role model and reference for me personally as well,' he told the club's website.

'I am excited to have that opportunity and enjoy learning from him, playing alongside him. With hard work, I think we can achieve good things together as a partnership and as a defence.'

Defence was an area which needed strengthening following the departure of Ibrahima Konate at the conclusion of his contract and the on-going injury issues at right-back.

Liverpool believe Araujo's experience – he was named Barcelona captain in January – is important and, significantly, he is up to speed having been involved in the Catalans' pre-season preparations and it is understood he will join squad training later this week.

He arrives having won three league titles with Barcelona, as well as two Copas del Rey, and wants to continue that at Anfield after the 2025 Premier League winners finished trophyless in a season which cost head coach Arne Slot his job just 12 months after lifting the title.

'Without a shadow of a doubt, the aim is to win trophies, win things. Liverpool is a team that is competing on all levels for all trophies, so we need to be battling it out on all fronts,' added Araujo, who has already received goodwill messages from two other Uruguayans who played for the club in Luis Suarez and Darwin Nunez.

'You aim high at a club like this – that's what we'll all be doing. As well as aiming high, I'll be giving everything that I can out there on the pitch to try to make that happen.'

Andoni Iraola has sought to address his defensive crisis with a number of centre halves injured

Araujo's arrival gives head coach Andoni Iraola greater depth in defence than his predecessor as new arrival Jeremy Jacquet is expected to return to training after a knee injury while Giovanni Leoni is entering the final stages of his rehabilitation following an ACL injury.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Ndiaye, both 18, have impressed in pre-season but with Joe Gomez not fit for the start of the new campaign, Iraola needed another senior defender as, for much of last season, Liverpool had to play Van Dijk and Konate virtually every game.

Liverpool are continuing to actively look for more signings, with attack in need of reinforcement, and Araujo's fee-free arrival will not impact those plans.

They have an interest in Paris St Germain's Bradley Barcola but will not pay over the odds, in keeping with their self-sustaining model of seeking value in the market.

Sports.title: Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg break down - with French club Marseille left furious at ex-Tottenham man's change of heart
Sports.content:
Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg break down - with French club Marseille left furious at ex-Tottenham man's change of heart

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Daily Mail Sport understands Marseille's owners have been left furious by this change of heart. The French club, keen to raise funds for their own summer spending, provisionally agreed to selling the Dane to the Toon.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, has also become a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Villa director of football Damian Vidagany told German outlet Bild: 'Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans. We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.'

Talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the Newcastle deal

They have also missed out on top targets including Spain winger Victor Munoz, who opted to join Liverpool

Villa lost 2-1 to Bayern in a pre-season friendly in Hong Kong over the weekend and Palhinha came on as a substitute.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, star forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, the manager who saved them from relegation before transforming them into a Champions League club and their 56-year major trophy drought, then stepped down on July 31.

They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

Howe has since been replaced by a Jaissle, who joins from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli. The 38-year-old's previous coaching experiences include a two-year spell at RB Salzburg preceded by a short-term stint at Austrian side Liefering.

They have recouped north of £250million following the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and have made five signings this summer - goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal and have also lost key players in Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon too

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace at the High Court following a controversial banner displayed at Selhurst Park last season.

The Nottingham Forest owner on Monday lodged a claim for defamation against his club’s Premier League rivals that dates back to the 1-1 draw between the clubs last August.

The banner depicting Marinakis holding a gun to the head of Forest player Morgan Gibbs-White and carried the words ‘Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.’ Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to such allegations.

Palace were charged by the Football Association last November and while the banner was not specified as the reason for the charge, there are strict rules regarding messaging containing defamatory, political and offensive slogans.

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago, due to UEFA’s rules regarding multi-club ownership. Forest benefited from that decision and were promoted into the Europa League.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is pursuing a defamation case against Crystal Palace

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago

The Gibbs-White/Marinakis banner appeared while that row was still fresh in the clubs’ minds.

Then Oliver Glasner, who led Palace to three trophies before departing at the end of last season, was promptly hired by Forest on a three-year deal. Palace host Forest in the Premier League on October 10.

‘This claim has been issued at Court shortly before the expiry of the one-year limitation period in defamation which could indicate that prior efforts to resolve the dispute have been unsuccessful,’ said Jamie Hurworth, a defamation specialist for law firm Payne Hicks Beach.

‘One of the first steps will be for the Court to determine how a reasonable reader would have interpreted the allegations on the banner which included an image of a gun being held to a player’s head, and whether that allegation is defamatory.

‘There will also be a potentially novel legal issue to address given the banner was held up by Crystal Palace fans, rather than perhaps any allegations being made by or on behalf of the club itself.’

Crystal Palace have declined to comment.

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Amy Hunt stormed to European Championships gold with a blistering effort in the 100m, finishing in 11 seconds flat - having been in fifth at the 50m mark.

It's the latest statement of intent in a burgeoning career that could see the Grantham-born sprinter reach the pinnacle of her sport.

Prior to her triumph on Monday night, Daily Mail Sport sat down with the 'sexy and aggressive' athlete on her remarkable rise.

Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Aston Villa dealt blow in loan pursuit of Real Madrid star Endrick - with Jose Mourinho making a decision on Brazilian forward's future
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's hopes of taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid have been dashed by the LaLiga club's decision to keep him.

The Brazilian forward's future had been in limbo, with the youngster waiting to see if he is part of Jose Mourinho's plans for this season as he wants to establish himself in Madrid.

Had Mourinho not included Endrick in his plans, he may have been forced to seek a temporary move away as he did last season with Lyon.

But Daily Mail Sport understands that the legendary former Chelsea boss wants to include Endrick in his first team plans moving forwards, dealing a hammer blow to any pursuit from Villa.

The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024 after he turned 18, with a deal having been agreed two years before.

He has scored seven goals in 40 appearances for Los Blancos but joined Lyon for the second half of 2025-26 after struggling for regular gametime.

Endrick impressed in France, netting five goals and adding seven assists in 16 appearances.

Aston Villa are among the list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid

Real boss Jose Mourinho is set to make a decision on the Brazilian forward in the near future

That form was enough for him to earn a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, yet despite significant clamour back home, the 20-year-old only played 111 minutes at the tournament.

Endrick failed to score during that time as Carlo Ancelotti's side suffered an embarrassing exit in the last-16 stage at the hands of Norway.

Villa are looking for attacking reinforcements following the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans this summer, while there is uncertainty over the future of backup striker Tammy Abraham.

Ollie Watkins was also linked with Fenerbahce last month and Unai Emery's side sold Lucas Digne to PSG over the weekend.

They have so far added Switzerland World Cup breakout star Johan Manzambi and Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes.

Emery's side kick off their season with the UEFA Super Cup against PSG on Wednesday night, before they travel to Brighton next weekend in the Premier League.

Sports.title: City still want Bouaddi, West Ham interested in signing free agent Jamie Vardy as striker prepares to return to England - and Newcastle talks with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg break down: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City not giving up on Bouaddi

Manchester City are continuing discussions with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is keen to join City now rather than wait another season, which was Lille's preference, and the clubs are working towards agreement on a fee.

City still want another midfielder for when Rodri joins Barcelona with talks ongoing over a fee for the Spain captain.

Tottenham are continuing to monitor developments with Omar Marmoush and Savinho while Nottingham Forest want Tijjani Reijnders.

City and Southampton have agreed a season-long loan deal for Divin Mubama, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport. The 21-year-old forward spent last season on loan at Stoke City making 28 appearances in all competitions prior to damaging ankle ligaments in January.

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen to join Man City this summer

Wrexham want Leeds forward Gelhardt

Leeds forward Joe Gelhardt is wanted by Wrexham in a £4.5million deal.

The 24-year-old has spent the past two seasons on loan at Hull City and played a key part in their Championship promotion campaign last season scoring 14 league goals.

Wrexham recognise he could play a similar role for them as they attempt to take the next big step up into the top flight.

Hull have also considered a return for Gelhardt but are working on other targets including Swansea City's Zan Vipotnik.

Chelsea line up LA Galaxy youngster

Chelsea are close to finalising a deal for 16-year-old LA Galaxy midfielder Vicente Garcia.

The deal is expected to be worth £2.25m plus add-ons and Garcia would join Chelsea when he turns 18 in 2028.

Hojbjerg talks with Toon break down

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, became a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Full story

The Denmark star is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested

Newcastle winger Murphy set for Kaiserslautern

Newcastle United defender Alex Murphy is on the verge of a season-long loan move to Kaiserslautern.

The Republic of Ireland U21 international, who can play centre-back and left-back, is having a medical ahead of joining the Bundesliga 2 club.

Liverpool's Morrison wanted by Groningen

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is attracting interest from FC Groningen among other clubs. The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international will be allowed to leave on loan.

Morrison, who started out at Manchester United, made his international debut in June against Guinea.

Tottenham winger off to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-hyeok is in talks to join Belgian side Westerlo. The 20-year-old, who joined Spurs in 2025, has had loan spells with QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry City since. The South Korea international is expected in Belgium today for his medical.

Hammers knocked back in Parrott pursuit

West Ham have had their opening bid for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott rejected.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Hammers made their opening offer of around £15million over the weekend but it is likely to take a Championship record fee of £17.5m to get their man. They are now formulating a new offer.

RB Leipzig have also contacted Alkmaar in recent days but the Hammers are further advanced.

West Ham are exploring a move for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson and have made an approach for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Tigers turned down in Vipotnik chase

Hull have had a bid rejected by Swansea for striker Zan Vipotnik.

The Premier League side's offer is understood to have fallen well short of Swansea's valuation of last season's Championship top scorer.

Palace keen on Khalaili

Crystal Palace's move for Union Saint-Gilloise right wing-back Anan Khalaili is progressing.

The Israeli international saw a £21million move to Inter Milan collapse over a medical issue but has had a number of clubs enquiring since.

Khalaili has had his medical ahead of signing a five-year deal.

Charles edges closer to Fulham switch

Shea Charles is undergoing his Fulham medical this morning ahead of his £30million transfer from Southampton.

Fulham have agreed to pay £27m with a further £3m in add-ons for the 22-year-old after Manchester City declined their option to activate matching rights.

Southampton retain a 20 per cent sell-on while Charles has agreed a five-year deal with an option for a further year.

McNeil and Johnson undergo medicals

Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson have undergone medicals and agreed four-year contracts ahead of their swap move to Crystal Palace and Everton respectively.

The clubs say no fees are involved despite McNeil having only one year left on contract and Johnson having four.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

McNeil nearly joined Palace on Deadline Day in January, but the £20m move broke down due to paperwork not being submitted in time.

Johnson has struggled to settle at Palace since joining from Tottenham for £35m in January. Everton have also held an interest in Johnson in previous windows.

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

Hammers approach Vardy

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

Leicester have signed goalkeeper Franco Ravizzoli on a free transfer from Blackpool.

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Araujo completes medical

Ronald Araujo has completed his Liverpool medical ahead of completing a loan move from Barcelona.

The 27-year-old's signing is expected to be announced this afternoon.

The Uruguay defender's loan also includes an option to buy for around £47.1m.

Villa keep tabs on Endrick

Aston Villa are among the growing list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid. The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected

Jamie Vardy is a man without a club after leaving Cremonese and West Ham have him on their shortlist as they seek to add a new striker before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy could find himself back in England at the age of 39

West Ham are considering making a move for veteran frontman Jamie Vardy if they are unsuccessful with their pursuit of Troy Parrott.

‌



The former Leicester City forward wants to remain playing and is a free agent after his contract with Italian side Cremonese expired. It was his first spell playing outside of England and the Hammers could present the 39-year-old with the chance to return.

‌



Currently West Ham, who are gearing up for a first year in the Championship for more than a decade, have their sights on Parrott, formerly of Tottenham. The Irishman is now playing for AZ Alkmaar, where he has scored 51 goals in his two seasons.

‌



The Times reports that they've had a bid of £15million rejected and, if the Dutch side hold firm and refuse to sell their striker, then it could open the door for Vardy to make a move to the London Stadium. Another player on their shortlist was Wilson Isidor, but Sunderland have insisted he is not leaving.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Vardy spent the bulk of his career with the Foxes and was on their books when they won promotion from the Championship in 2014, he scored 16 times that year. Within two years he was a Premier League winner and proved himself to be a prolific marksman in the top flight.

Vardy scored 145 times in the top flight, putting him 14th on the all-time list, whilst he also won the Golden Boot in 2020. The former Fleetwood striker would win another Championship title with Leicester in 2022, scoring 20 times, and his experience could prove an asset for the Hammers as they seek an immediate return to the Premier League.

‌



The Hammers have just announced the signing of Manor Solomon, who penned a three-year deal after finalising a £7m switch from Tottenham. The winger was on loan at Leeds when they won promotion from the Championship in 2025.

View 2 Images West Ham are currently chasing Troy Parrott, but AZ Alkmaar have rejected their bids so far

West Ham are heavy favourites to win the Championship. They've managed to retain England international Jarrod Bowen whilst Nuno Espirito Santo has chosen to remain as manager. He won the second tier with Wolves back in 2017.

Article continues below

The Hammers began their season by beating Portsmouth in the first round of the Carabao Cup at the weekend. They will play fellow relegated side Burnley on Sunday at Turf Moor as they kick off their Championship campaign with one of their more challenging fixtures.

Sports.title: 9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem
Sports.content:
It's been a summer of upheaval in the Premier League, with nearly half of the 20 sides opting to change manager in the off-season.

Clubs at both ends of the spectrum have put their faith in a new boss in the hope that the 2026/27 season will bring success. Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea have all changed tack, albeit for differing reasons, with Enzo Maresca chosen to succeed Pep Guardiola, while Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso have walked in after frustrating campaigns under previous coaches.

Fulham, Nottingham Forest, Ipswich, Crystal Palace, Newcastle and Bournemouth also have fresh - but in some cases familiar - faces in the dugout. They know just how high the stakes are, especially at Forest, who burnt through four managers last season.

It is extremely unlikely that all nine new bosses will see their plans come to fruition in the coming months, so who will sink and who will swim? Here Mirror Football attempts to rank them in terms of which has the best chance of achieving their goals.

‌



9. Fulham - Alvaro Arbeloa

Marco Silva left Fulham this summer for Benfica having achieved one of the most boringly successful, under-the-radar stints in Premier League managerial history. After bringing Fulham up as champions in 2021/22, he embarked upon (depending on your viewpoint) mid-table security or mid-table mediocrity: 10th, 13th, 11th, 11th. In short, he did a good job but without pulling up trees.

It is into this context that Arbeloa walks, the Real Madrid cast-off attempting to establish himself. I would suggest that signing two other Real Madrid cast-offs, in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, may not have been the best way to try and move on from your past.

Harry Wilson, Fulham's stand-out player from last season, and Raul Jimenez, their experienced striker, have both left. We have no evidence yet that Arbeloa has the tactical nous to craft a new playing style, or the force of personality to create a team bond. I fear they are going to struggle.

View 7 Images Alvaro Arbeloa may struggle at Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



8. Newcastle - Matthias Jaissle

You fear for Jaissle - and not because of anything he has done (yet). Newcastle have undergone a huge turnover this summer, selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, while also seeing Eddie Howe resign.

Howe was in situ for nearly five years and his exit was always going to cause instability. The fact his exit came alongside the departures of three key players means Newcastle are at risk of spiralling downwards after their 12th-place finish last season.

The Magpies' owners, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, have promised a lot and Jaissle is their man, having been recruited from the relative obscurity of Al-Ahli. Just 38 years old, the German has landed an exciting job, but an extremely difficult one.

Their new signings this summer fall into the camp of 'plenty of potential' rather than 'proven performers'. There is still some time to add some players from the latter section, but reports that Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has turned down the chance to join them suggests their transfer window woes could continue.

‌



View 7 Images Matthias Jaissle is the new man in charge at Newcastle (Image: 2026 Newcastle United)

7. Ipswich - Gary O'Neil

It's hard to judge O'Neil following a rollercoaster few years in management. But he won't have much time to settle in at Portman Road, having stepped into the breach following Kieran McKenna's surprise decision to walk away after leading the Tractor Boys to promotion.

O'Neil's star rose due to his spell at Bournemouth, fell after his time at Wolves - despite actually having a better win percentage - and then plateaued at Chelsea sister club Strasbourg. So is he one of the brightest English coaches in the game, or a middle-of-the-road one who has been over-promoted? We're about to get a better idea.

6. Liverpool - Andoni Iraola

View 7 Images Andoni Iraola has lots of problems to contend with (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola is obviously a brilliant coach and man-manager. His time at Bournemouth, in which he consistently improved the side, despite losing star after star to bigger clubs, earned him a shot at the big time. But pre-season has shown just how difficult the task is that he inherited from Arne Slot.

There are issues all over the pitch to address - from an ageing and injured central defence, through a central midfield which has lost its trademark high-energy pressing, to a misfiring (and extremely expensive) attack.

The job at Anfield is totally different to the one which the Spaniard became used to with the Cherries. He will have to manage egos, deal with heightened expectations, juggle the squad to cope with the Champions League, and - ultimately - win games straight away.

That will take time. This won't be a quick fix.

‌



5. Nottingham Forest - Oliver Glasner

Nuno Espirito Santo. Ange Postecoglou. Sean Dyche. Vitor Pereira. Forest went through all of them last season and still somehow managed to stay in the Premier League.

Glasner attracted plenty of interest when he announced he would leave Crystal Palace at the end of the season and eventually landed in Nottingham, where he will hope to buck the trend of notoriously impatient owner Evangelos Marinakis.

Glasner showed at Palace that he is an extremely shrewd operator with a clear playing style. He can drill players into his way of doing things. But, as we saw during his final months at Palace, he is not shy in voicing his frustrations when it comes to transfers. If he decides to take on Marinakis then it will only go one way.

View 7 Images Oliver Glasner has a completely different environment to deal with at Forest (Image: PA)

‌



4. Crystal Palace - Pierre Sage

The 47-year-old Frenchman arrived in south London after a seriously impressive one and only season with Lens, who he led to the Coupe de France final - the club's first since 1998 - and second place in Ligue 1.

The question is whether his success in France will translate into the Premier League with Palace following the successful reign of Glasner. Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira are proof that it doesn't always work out like Glasner when taking a manager from abroad.

Sage worked in academy football for years before ascending to first-team football. He is a calm head and will take a methodical approach with Palace, which should mean a steady succession.

3. Chelsea - Xabi Alonso

View 7 Images Xabi Alonso has a huge squad to whittle down at Chelsea (Image: Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Getty Images)

‌



Alonso knows how hard it could be for him. "I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," he said this summer. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them."

The Spaniard has been handed more control than his predecessors, which is shown by his "manager" title, rather than "head coach". He failed at Real Madrid, but was extremely impressive at Bayer Leverkusen and has a ludicrously stacked squad with which to create his own identity at Chelsea.

While some managers have found the Blues' embarrassment of riches a hindrance, preferring a smaller squad, Alonso could be the man to tame it. If he can strike the right balance, maintaining squad harmony while honing in on those players who suit his style, they could be onto a winner.

2. Bournemouth - Marco Rose

Bournemouth's reputation for being a well-run club is fully deserved. Their recruitment team continually strike gold when scouring the market for young, talented and under-valued players. That - plus Iraola's coaching - has allowed them to continue to thrive despite selling those players on a few years later.

‌



Rose has worked at Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, so has experience of 'bigger' clubs than Bournemouth. While he hasn't lasted long at either of the German giants, he has been hired due to his reputation as a coach who can get the best out of young players. Given their track record, I trust Bournemouth's judgement.

1. Manchester City - Enzo Maresca

View 7 Images Enzo Maresca has been groomed as Pep Guardiola's successor for some time

Pep Guardiola's successor has been groomed for many years for the role. Having worked under the City boss as a coach and soaked up his tactical philosophy, Maresca could hardly be more of a continuity pick.

The Italian left Chelsea under a cloud, but he has everything in place at City to succeed. Yes, following long-serving successful bosses is difficult, as David Moyes showed at Manchester United following Sir Alex Ferguson's departure. Maresca isn't walking into something unknown. He knows the club, he knows the players and he knows exactly what's expected of him in the City set-up. He's not Pep, but things aren't about to drop off a cliff.

‌

Sports.title: Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'
Sports.content:
Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'

Arsenal eyed up a blockbuster move for Vinicius Junior this summer but the Real Madrid star ultimately decided to stay put - and the Premier League side have since been mocked

View 2 Images Jon Obi Mikel has poked fun at Arsenal's standing as they looked to prise Vinicius Jnr from Real Madrid (Image: The Obi One Podcast)

Arsenal have been told they're not "one of the big boys" by John Obi Mikel, who has mocked them for believing they could ever sign Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Gunners were heavily linked with the Brazilian earlier this summer in what would've been a club-record move. Vinicius' contract was winding down and the Premier League champions were looking to seize on the uncertainty.

‌



It would've been a blockbuster transfer had Arsenal pulled it off, but the player ultimately decided to extend his stay at the Bernabeu, leaving the north Londoners to look elsewhere in a bid to bolster their forward line.

‌



But Mikel has laughed off the idea that Vinicius was ever going to move to Arsenal, insisting the club have got above their station after winning a first league title in two decades whilst still awaiting their first ever Champions League triumph.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

The former Chelsea midfielder said on The Obi One Podcast: "I don’t know what the Arsenal fans were expecting. You win the league after 22 years and then you all of a sudden think: that’s it, you’ve arrived, you’re one of the big boys again. No, you’re not.

"They’ve just been humbled because I said it: there’s no way Vinicius Junior is leaving Real Madrid to go to Arsenal, a club that’s won one title in 22 years. This guy wins titles, he’s won lots of titles at Real Madrid. He wants to win titles season after season, the Champions League, La Liga, competing year after year and winning those titles.

‌



"He’s tasted what it feels like winning the Champions League, Arsenal have never won the Champions League. Zero. You expect a player who has won the Champions League with Real Madrid to leave that."

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr has chosen to remain with Real Madrid (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Mikel believes that Real Madrid, who have Jose Mourinho at the helm once again, are assembling a team that can challenge for Europe's highest honour once again. They've already signed the likes of Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva and Yan Diomande.

Article continues below

Arsenal meanwhile have looked to build on their champion year and added Bruno Guimaraes at the weekend. The former Newcastle midfielder is their biggest capture of the summer so far, at £75m, and they're still in the market for a major frontline signing.

Sports.title: Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp

Rangers have endured a winless start to the season under new boss Derek McInnes but their chief executive has compared him to Jurgen Klopp in a shareholders meeting

View 2 Images Derek McInnes is yet to win as Rangers boss

Rangers shareholders were told to see Derek McInnes as "a Jurgen Klopp-type manager" by chief executive Jim Gillespie as he defended the under fire boss.

‌



McInnes was appointed at Ibrox off the back of a stellar spell at Hearts, that saw him come within minutes of winning the Scottish title last year, only to be upset by Celtic in a dramatic final day. They were still able to finish above Rangers, who quickly moved to hire him.

‌



However, Rangers have endured a poor start to the season and Sunday's defeat at home to Hibernian means they are already five points off the pace set by bitter rivals Celtic after only two games.

‌



The Scottish giants have held a meeting of their shareholders and Gillespie's comparison of McInnes and Klopp has raised eyebrows. The German has just taken charge of his national side but is regarded among the greatest managers of the modern era.

When asked by a shareholder to explain what attracted the club to the McInnes Gillespie replied: “You have two types of managers — a Klopp-type manager and a [Pep] Guardiola type. We think Derek is a Klopp type, someone who plays front-foot football and wants to win. Derek is the only manager who ticked all our boxes.”

McInnes didn't attend the meeting, and when pressed on that club chief Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago but McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team, who are in Europa League qualifying action on Thursday.

‌



The new Rangers boss has come out fighting following their slow start and maintains that the team are not as bad as the outside noise suggests.

View 2 Images Klopp won the Premier League with Liverpool and is regarded as one of their greatest managers (Image: LAURENCE GRIFFITHS/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"We're not as bad as some people will be saying at the minute," he told Sky Sports. "And I think it's important that we just batten down the hatches, stay strong, stay together. We try, as a club, to come out of this window strong and we will.

Article continues below

"At the minute, we're trying to manage the situation. Some players are not quite as fit but we need to get them playing to get them fit. We're not at the start we wanted but we still plan to get the finish and the outcome that we want and we'll work towards that."
