Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs. Lucas Bahdi Get Another Week to Avoid Purse Bid
Sports.content:
“The purse bid for the vacant WBA Lightweight World Championship bout between Floyd Schofield and Lucas Bahdi, which was scheduled to take place this Tuesday, August 11, has been postponed at the request of both parties, who asked for additional time as they continue working toward an agreement,” the WBA stated Monday.

For Schofield, 23, this is a valuable opening in a lightweight division filled with difficult fights. He can become a world champion without having to go through WBC champion William Zepeda, WBO champion Abdullah Mason, or IBF champion Raymond Muratalla. At this stage of his career, getting a direct title opportunity without first eliminating another top contender is about as favorable a position as Schofield could want.

Bahdi has his own opportunity. The Canadian made his biggest impression by knocking out Ashton Sylve in the fifth round in July 2024. He now has the chance to turn that victory into something considerably bigger.

The fact that both camps requested the extension is encouraging for the fight getting made. They have until August 18 to complete an agreement before the purse-bid process resumes.

Sports.title: Zayas Loss Leads Abass Baraou To Top Rank
Sports.content:
That move says plenty about how Top Rank viewed Baraou in defeat.

“Abass Baraou’s recent performances speak for themselves,” Top Rank President Todd duBoef said. “He defied the odds by dominating Yoenis Tellez for the interim world title, was soon elevated to full champion, and came within a narrow split decision of unifying titles against Xander Zayas in January.”

Baraou (17-2, 9 KOs) had already built a solid reputation before that unification bout. He earned the WBA interim belt by scoring a late knockdown during a unanimous decision win over Yoenis Tellez last August, then was elevated to full champion after Terence Crawford vacated.

The Zayas fight gave Top Rank an opportunity to evaluate Baraou against one of its own champions. Although Zayas won, Baraou showed over 12 rounds that he belongs among the better fighters at 154 pounds.

Baraou will not receive a soft touch in his promotional debut. The 31-year-old meets Giovani Santillan in a 10-round main event September 11 in Oceanside, California.

A win over Santillan would give Top Rank another reason to keep Baraou near the top of the division. With Zayas under the same promotional banner, a second fight would also be considerably easier to make if Baraou earns his way back.

Sports.title: Noel Mikaelian Calls Jai Opetaia Fight Cruiserweight’s True Championship
Sports.content:
“Jai is the legitimate IBF champion, and I’m the legitimate WBC champion. So it’s the two real cruiserweight champions colliding,” Mikaelian said to The Ring.

Opetaia no longer holds the IBF title, but Mikaelian’s larger argument is clear. He sees himself alongside the Australian at the top of the division rather than among the fighters trying to establish themselves beneath him. That hierarchy hasn’t been settled.

David Benavidez has inserted himself into the discussion after moving up in weight to win the WBA and WBO titles, but his position relative to the other leading cruiserweights remains uncertain. The same applies to Mikaelian. His WBC championship gives him credibility, but it doesn’t establish him as Opetaia’s closest rival.

Mikaelian believes his history with Briedis strengthens his case. When Opetaia’s accomplishments against the former champion were mentioned during the interview, he quickly brought up their 2018 fight.

“I beat Briedis too though,” Mikaelian said.

Mikaelian officially lost that fight by unanimous decision, although he has long maintained that he deserved the win.

September 12 gives him something far more useful than arguing about an eight-year-old verdict. If Mikaelian beats Opetaia, he won’t need a belt or the Briedis fight to support his case.

Opetaia has already proven where he belongs at cruiserweight, but Mikaelian still has to do it.

Sports.title: Bradley Wants Jaron Ennis To Clean Out 160 For Terence Crawford
Sports.content:
“Boots ain’t got [anything] that Crawford needs, nothing at all,” Bradley said on his channel. “Well, Boots go up, if you go up to 160 and you wipe out the whole division there and you win all the straps there, maybe that might be enticing.”

That’s a steep demand for a fighter who recently moved to 154.

Cleaning out 160 could mean Ennis having to go through Carlos Adames, Denzel Bentley and Aaron McKenna. Yoenli Hernandez presents an additional obstacle if the dangerous Cuban gets his hands on one of the belts.

Even 43-year-old Erislandy Lara isn’t necessarily an easy night. His age is considerable, but his Cuban amateur schooling, sharp timing and technical ability have allowed him to remain effective long after most fighters decline.

Getting the necessary fights wouldn’t happen overnight, either. Ennis could spend close to 24 months satisfying Bradley’s demand, assuming the champions are willing to fight him and negotiations move quickly.

Yet Bradley doesn’t believe Crawford needs those two years to prepare for Boots. He thinks Crawford destroys him today.

“Crawford would knock the dog [expletive] out of Boots Ennis,” Bradley said. “I’m telling y’all right now.”

Bradley later predicted a “brutal” knockout, criticizing Ennis for lunging, rushing his attacks and fighting without enough discipline.

That leaves an obvious question. If Boots is easy work for Crawford today, why should he first have to conquer a middleweight division containing fighters who would present serious challenges for Crawford himself?

Bradley’s demand doesn’t make Crawford-Ennis more attractive. It potentially delays the fight until Crawford is around 40 and Boots has spent another two years developing against bigger men.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Draws 748,000 Viewers On TNT
Sports.content:
The network reported that Zepeda-Roach pulled in 748,000 viewers, while the IBF lightweight title fight between Raymond Muratalla and Robson Conceição generated 738,000. The telecast peaked at 786,000 during the championship portion of the card.

Those numbers are encouraging for Zepeda because he was not relying on a major mainstream attraction on the other side of the ring. Roach had gained attention from his controversial draw against Gervonta Davis, but neither fighter has been established as a major television draw.

The entire August 1 telecast registered an average of 598,000 viewers. More importantly, the final two hours averaged 694,000, a 2% increase over the inaugural July 4 boxing show.

That first card peaked at 820,000 viewers, meaning the August 1 peak was slightly lower. However, the higher average over the final two hours indicates viewers stayed with the championship fights once they began.

Zepeda defeated Roach by scores of 117-111, 117-111 and 118-110 to capture the vacant WBC lightweight title. He now has an obvious unification possibility against WBO champion Abdullah Mason, who headlined the first The Fight card with his July 4 victory over Albert Bell.

Putting Mason and Zepeda together would allow the network to match the winners of its first two main events while both champions are already familiar to viewers of the series.

Sports.title: Teremoana Still Five Or Six Fights From Title Shot
Sports.content:
“I think he’s probably five or six fights away from challenging for a world title,” Hearn told Raw Sports Media. “There’s many levels between DeAndre Savage and Joshua and Fury and those kind of guys, but he’s 11-0 now, so I think get him to 15, 16-0 and we’re going to have to find someone.”

The question is why he needs that much time.

This is not a young heavyweight learning how he wants to fight. His aggressive style was already established during his amateur career and remains largely unchanged as a professional. At the 2024 Olympics, he aggressively pursued Bakhodir Jalolov rather than treating the experienced Uzbek with excessive respect.

Two years later, the Australian Teremona is still overwhelming opponents with the same mix of size, speed, aggression and power.

The missing test is an opponent capable of surviving long enough to force something different from him.

“We’re going to have to find someone who can take him five, six, seven, eight, nine rounds, but it’s very difficult to stand up to the firepower,” Hearn said.

That sounds more like an argument for accelerating the competition than extending his development for another two years.

Hearn admits there is still a lot to learn about how Teremoana responds against a rugged heavyweight who can force him into a difficult fight. He believes Teremoana possesses the chin and heart required, but short fights haven’t provided the opportunity to demonstrate either.

Another series of opponents who disappear within two rounds won’t answer those questions. A serious contender might.

Teremoana’s greatest weapons are physical ones, and there is little reason to spend his late twenties protecting them. If he is as dangerous as he looks, the quickest way to find out is to start matching him like it.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Exposed Canelo Alvarez’s Carefully Managed Career
Sports.content:
Gennadiy Golovkin spent years pursuing Canelo before finally getting him in the ring at 35. Their first fight ended in a controversial draw, with many observers believing Golovkin deserved the decision.

Canelo’s 2019 move to light heavyweight provided another example. He challenged 36-year-old Sergey Kovalev for the WBO title rather than Artur Beterbiev, who held the WBC and IBF belts after stopping Oleksandr Gvozdyk.

The same criticism followed Canelo at 168. Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga and William Scull received fights while more dangerous younger contenders remained outside his schedule.

That history provides some perspective on Crawford’s accomplishment. Canelo had spent much of his career operating from a position where his team could choose the opponent and timing. Crawford stepped into that environment. He took away the advantages careful matchmaking had helped preserve.

McIntyre had seen through the aura years earlier. Once Crawford finally got the opportunity, Canelo proved to be the fighter BoMac had always believed his pupil could solve.

Sports.title: Abdullah Mason vs William Zepeda Is The Fight TNT Needs
Sports.content:
“Not sure if ‘The Fight’ can generate the same impact that ‘Boxing After Dark’ had during its prime, but this fight would go a very long way to further validating the series. Both winning big on its first two shows, a head-on collision is the natural next course of action,” said Donovan on X.

There are no negotiations for Mason-Zepeda at this stage, but Mason has already made it clear that he likes the matchup. The 22-year-old recently described Zepeda as the type of opponent who can give him a career-defining fight. Zepeda brings relentless pressure and an enormous punch output, presenting Mason with a much tougher physical test than Bell did.

The first two broadcasts introduced Mason and Zepeda separately. Putting them together next would give viewers a reason to follow the series from one card to another rather than treating each event as an unrelated main event.

Boxing After Dark developed its reputation by giving fighters difficult fights and bringing successful performers back against increasingly dangerous opposition. The Fight doesn’t need to duplicate HBO’s old formula, but Mason against Zepeda would be a strong place to start building its own.

Ghana News.title: “I’m not sure” – K.T Hammond unsure if OSP has questioned Kwabena Donkor over Berko bribery case
Ghana News.content:
Former Power Minister Dr Kwabena Donkor’s lawyer says he is unsure whether his client has been contacted by Ghana’s Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) or US authorities following the conviction of former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko.

K.T. Hammond gave the response during an interview with JoyNews when asked whether Dr Donkor had been approached by investigators in connection with the bribery case.

“I’m not sure,” he responded.

The uncertainty comes against the backdrop of the OSP’s confirmed involvement in the US investigation that culminated in Berko’s conviction.

The OSP has disclosed that it provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) through Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework.

Berko was convicted by a US federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, on charges linked to a scheme in which more than US$1 million in bribes were paid to Ghanaian officials in connection with the development and financing of a power plant involving Aksa Energy.

The disclosure of the OSP’s role has heightened interest in whether evidence gathered during the US investigation could lead to further action against individuals in Ghana.

Dr Donkor, who was Power Minister during the period of the transaction, has denied any involvement in the alleged bribery.

His lawyer has maintained that the former minister never met Berko, never negotiated with him and never demanded or received money from him in connection with the deal.

Meanwhile, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has intensified its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the case, with asset tracing and recovery forming part of its investigative plan.

The Attorney-General has also directed EOCO to escalate its investigations as relevant information and official records are obtained from US authorities.

For now, Dr Donkor maintains that he had no role in the alleged bribery scheme and says he never had any dealings with Berko.

Ghana News.title: Istanbul trip was standard due diligence for Aksa power deal – K.T. Hammond
Ghana News.content:
A lawyer for former Power Minister Dr Kwabena Donkor, K.T. Hammond has defended the decision by a Ghanaian technical team to travel to Istanbul, Turkey, to inspect equipment linked to the controversial Aksa Energy power deal.

K.T. Hammond said the trip was part of the standard technical due diligence required before major power-generation equipment was shipped to Ghana.

Speaking to JoyNews, the lawyer said it was necessary for Ghanaian officials to physically inspect the equipment and establish that it met the required standards and could deliver the expected generation capacity.

“The procedure would always be to get the technical people to go on site and inspect and be sure about the sanctity and integrity of the equipment you are receiving,” he said.

His comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the Aksa Energy deal following the conviction in the United States of former Tema Oil Refinery Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko for his role in a bribery scheme involving Ghanaian officials.

Berko was convicted by a US federal jury on charges linked to the payment of more than US$1 million in bribes to Ghanaian officials in connection with the development and financing of a power plant in Ghana.

Dr Donkor, who was Minister for Power at the time of the transaction, has denied receiving any money or having any dealings with Berko.

His lawyer maintained that the Istanbul inspection was not a political exercise but an institutional process involving technical personnel from relevant agencies in Ghana's power sector.

He said the country was seeking to bring in about 370 megawatts of generating capacity at a time when Ghana was facing a severe power crisis, popularly known as Dumsor.

According to Mr Hammond, technical verification was therefore critical to ensure the equipment being supplied was fit for purpose.

“You bring some plant, and they look at it, and they say, well, it's anthracnose, or whatever you're looking for, and they can't do the job. So what do we do?” he asked.

He explained that the inspection involved representatives from various stakeholders in Ghana's electricity sector, including the Volta River Authority (VRA).

The lawyer's comments seek to provide context to one of the key processes surrounding the emergency power arrangement at the centre of the US bribery case.

The Aksa Energy deal was concluded during Ghana's prolonged power crisis, when the government was seeking additional generation capacity to address persistent electricity shortages.

The US prosecution of Berko has since triggered renewed calls for scrutiny of the Ghanaian side of the transaction, including the conduct of officials who were involved in negotiating, approving or facilitating the deal.

However, Mr Hammond insists Dr Donkor should not be held responsible for any alleged misconduct by individuals who may have acted independently or invoked his name without authorisation.

“If anybody goes on the frolic of their own and makes some scandalous and criminal demands on his behalf, he did not provide that,” he said.

Dr Donkor served as Power Minister during the period in which the deal was negotiated and later resigned from government on December 31, 2015.

He has categorically denied ever meeting Berko, demanding money from him or receiving any payment connected to the transaction.

The Office of the Special Prosecutor has previously disclosed that it provided investigative assistance to US authorities in the Berko case.

The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has also begun investigations into the Ghanaian dimension of the matter, including tracing potential assets or proceeds connected to suspected criminal conduct.

Mr Hammond's account, however, is that the trip was a legitimate technical inspection undertaken as part of Ghana's efforts to urgently secure reliable power-generation equipment during the Dumsor crisis.

Ghana News.title: Kwabena Donkor never met Asante Berko, demanded or received money – K.T. Hammond
Ghana News.content:
Former Power Minister Dr Kwabena Donkor has denied ever meeting convicted former Goldman Sachs banker Asante Berko or demanding or receiving money in connection with the controversial Aksa Energy power deal.

His lawyer, K.T. Hammond, told JoyNews on Top Story that Dr Donkor has categorically rejected allegations linking him to the bribery scheme that led to Berko’s conviction in the United States.

“He has never met me. He never dealt with it,” Mr Hammond said, reading from instructions he said he had received from his client.

“He didn’t meet this man. He never negotiated with him. He never made any demands. It’s all there. It’s categorical denials. A, B, C, D, E.”

The lawyer’s comments come after a US federal jury convicted Asante Berko on August 6, 2026, over a bribery scheme involving Ghanaian officials and a power plant deal connected to Aksa Energy.

Berko, a former Goldman Sachs investment banker who later served as Managing Director of Tema Oil Refinery, was found guilty of conspiracy to violate the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, violating the Act and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

US prosecutors said Berko paid more than US$1 million in bribes between 2014 and 2015 to multiple Ghanaian officials in connection with the development and financing of the power project.

Dr Donkor was Power Minister during the period under scrutiny and resigned from office on December 31, 2015.

Mr Hammond maintained that his client's position was unambiguous and rejected suggestions that the denial could be interpreted to leave room for questions about payments allegedly made in Dr Donkor’s name.

“What is that supposed to mean? Read what is there,” he told JoyNews.

“I mean, this interpretation and asking me does that also mean what? It is there in clear terms, crystal clear. What he told me is what you are reading.”

When pressed on whether alleged payments made by persons connected to the transaction had come to Dr Donkor’s attention, the lawyer declined to accept the premise of the question.

“Could you ask another serious person? Don’t be flippant about this matter. We’re dealing with serious matters. Please,” he said.

While denying wrongdoing by his client, Mr Hammond confirmed Dr Donkor’s role as Power Minister at the time and defended the technical inspection of power-generation equipment in Istanbul, Turkey.

He said such an inspection was a normal part of the due diligence required for a major infrastructure project, particularly given Ghana’s electricity crisis at the time.

“So the procedure would always be to get the technical people to go on site and inspect and be sure about the sanctity and integrity of the equipment you are receiving,” he explained.

According to him, Ghana was acquiring about 370 megawatts of generating equipment during a period of severe power shortages, making technical verification important before the equipment was shipped.

He said the delegation included representatives from various stakeholders in Ghana’s electricity sector, including the Volta River Authority.

Mr Hammond further argued that Dr Donkor could not be held responsible if individuals independently used his name to make improper demands.

“If anybody goes on the frolic of their own and makes some scandalous and criminal demands on his behalf, he did not provide that,” he said.

“Those individuals would have done it for their own benefit, and he cannot be held responsible for that.”

The argument seeks to distinguish Dr Donkor from the conduct of any third parties who may have been involved in the bribery scheme.

Dr Donkor himself has not been charged with any offence in connection with the case.

Asked whether the former minister had been contacted by Ghana’s Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) or US authorities, Mr Hammond said he was unsure.

“I’m not sure,” he responded.

The OSP has previously disclosed that it provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) under Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework in the case that culminated in Berko’s conviction.

The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has also intensified its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the case, including asset tracing and recovery.

The Attorney-General has directed EOCO to escalate its investigations as relevant information and official records are obtained from US authorities.

For now, Dr Donkor maintains that he had no involvement in the alleged bribery and that he never met Berko, negotiated with him or received money from him.

The former minister’s denial comes as Ghanaian authorities continue examining evidence emerging from the US proceedings and assess whether any individuals in Ghana may have breached the law.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s refining capacity yet to shield fuel market from global shocks – CEMSE
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s growing refining capacity will improve fuel security but cannot yet fully shield the country from global petroleum market shocks, Benjamin Nsiah, an energy expert, has said.

He said local refineries operating at full capacity could meet about 60 per cent of current domestic petroleum demand, leaving the country dependent on imports for the remainder.

Mr Nsiah, Executive Director of the Centre for Environmental Management and Sustainable Energy (CEMSE), made the observation in an interview with the Ghana News Agency in Accra.

He said Ghana currently consumed between 120,000 and 140,000 barrels of petroleum products daily, making investments in local refining infrastructure important to strengthening energy security.

“At full capacity, looking at our current consumption of about 120,000 barrels a day to 140,000 barrels a day, they are likely going to do about 60 per cent of our daily demand,” he said.

Mr Nsiah therefore disagreed with suggestions that the operationalisation of new refineries alone would completely insulate Ghana from international fuel price fluctuations.

He said the country’s petroleum pricing regime remained exposed to international market developments because a significant proportion of refined petroleum products was still imported.

Mr Nsiah noted that under the deregulated pricing system, pump prices were largely influenced by international refined petroleum product prices, the exchange rate of the Ghana cedi against the United States dollar, freight and insurance costs, and statutory taxes and levies.

He said fluctuations in global oil prices and foreign exchange rates could therefore continue to affect domestic fuel prices despite efforts to expand local refining capacity.

Mr Nsiah said recent developments in both state-owned and private refineries offered prospects for increased domestic production.

He cited the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR), which recently announced a profit after tax of GH¢1.24 billion amid reforms aimed at strengthening its operations and contribution to national energy security.

Mr Nsiah said planned expansion projects by local refining companies could significantly increase domestic output and potentially enable Ghana to meet its entire fuel requirement.

“If they are able to do, as TOR has proposed, about an additional 100,000 barrels, and Sentuo is also adding, then these two companies will likely be able to exhaust our daily demand and even export,” he stated.

Mr Nsiah said achieving such capacity would put Ghana on a stronger path towards petroleum self-sufficiency and could enable the country to export petroleum products within the West African sub-region.

He also recommended that Ghana gradually recalibrate its petroleum pricing framework as domestic refining capacity expanded to reflect local refinery costs and operational realities.

Mr Nsiah said a stronger domestic refining industry would create an opportunity to reduce dependence on international pricing benchmarks that significantly influence fuel prices.

He said the long-term objective should be to build a resilient petroleum sector that ensures fuel availability while reducing the impact of external market disruptions on consumers and businesses.

Ghana News.title: New train service connects Finland and Sweden for first time in decades
Ghana News.content:
A new passenger train linking Finland and Sweden has begun running, creating the first rail connection between northern Finland and southern Europe in nearly 40 years.

Shortly after 05:00 local time (04:00 BST) on Monday, a double-decker train set off from the coastal Finnish city of Oulu, rumbling its way across the border to Sweden.

As the inaugural service crossed the Torne river from Finland and pulled into Sweden's Haparanda station, it was met by crowds of people waving Finnish and Swedish flags.

The route was initially suspended in the late 1980s to the early 1990s due to low passenger numbers and technical differences in the tracks between Finland and Europe.

Finland uses the same track widths as Russia, which are wider than the European standard - a holdover from when the Nordic nation was part of the Russian Grand Duchy in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

It is currently in the process of updating its track widths to match the European standard.

The new, twice-daily journey to Sweden's Haparanda takes 100-minutes as it hugs the west coast of Finland before crossing the border between the two Nordic neighbours.

Passengers travelling on from Haparanda will need to transfer onto a different train to continue southward.

But the service makes it possible to travel around 5,000km by rail from Portugal's Algarve to Finland's northernmost train station of Kolari - believed to be the longest train route in Europe.

It will also enable a 24-hour train journey between capitals Helsinki and Stockholm.

Finland's transport minister said the return of the cross-border service shows cooperation between the two countries was growing "all the time".

Elisa Markula, chief executive of Finland's state-owned railway operator VR, said she hopes the service will benefit from a "renaissance" in rail travel across Europe.

"Train travelling in all Europe is having a renaissance. Also in Finland, our passenger numbers are increasing a lot," Markula told AFP.

Nollywood actress Tonto Dikeh, on Sunday unveiled a new spiritual movement, the New Wine Prophetic Tabernacle.

Announcing the development via a post on her Instagram page, Dikeh described NWPT as an interdenominational altar and “global movement of consecrated believers called to experience the raw power, purity, and presence of God,” anchored on the biblical passage in Mark 2:22, which reads, “And no one puts new wine into old wineskins.”

It read in part, “NWPT exists as a dwelling place of His presence for those who refuse to settle for lukewarm Christianity and are hungry for genuine revival, fire, and transformation.”

Outlining its vision, the statement said the movement aims “to see a global awakening of consecrated believers operating in the raw power, purity, and presence of God transforming nations and establishing the Kingdom of Christ on Earth.”

On its mission, it stated that NWPT exists “to build an interdenominational altar of prayer, revival, and apostolic training that equips watchmen, activates spiritual gifts, drives relentless soul winning, and delivers total freedom to the captive through the power of the Holy Spirit.

The post further distinguished the gathering from a conventional church, stating, “This is not a church; it is an intense gathering of those consecrated and equipped for God. A people set apart, refined by His presence, and commissioned to advance His Kingdom.”

According to the announcement, NWPT holds weekly fellowship every Friday by 6:00pm.

Sunday’s announcement is coming months after the actress began signing many of her posts as “Ada El-Roi” and became active in Pastor Jerry Eze’s NSPPD community, amid widely reported changes to her dressing and public lifestyle.

PUNCHONLINE reports that in December 2025, Dikeh had shared a public testimony describing her deliverance from smoking, alcohol addiction, masturbation and prolonged anger issues during a service at Streams of Joy International Church, telling the congregation that she started smoking at age 13 and that God had healed her of the other struggles.

The actress, who ventured into politics in 2022 as a governorship running mate in Rivers State, had earlier in 2026 reflected on her turbulent marriage to her ex-husband, Olakunle Churchill, ten years after their public separation, months before the pair reconciled publicly, ending their long-running feud.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Seventy years after South Africa’s women’s march, the struggle is not over
World.content:
Women helped defeat apartheid’s pass laws, but many still face violence, poverty and unemployment.

Johannesburg, South Africa – Seventy years ago, Sophie Williams-de Bruyn was 18 when she joined about 20,000 women marching to the Union Buildings, the seat of South Africa’s apartheid government, to protest against the extension of the pass laws to Black women.

On August 9, 1956, the women gathered in Pretoria carrying a petition against laws that restricted the movement of Black South Africans. Williams-de Bruyn was among the leaders of the march, which became one of the defining moments of the country’s liberation struggle.

On Sunday, at 88, she returned to the same grounds.

The country around her had changed. Apartheid had ended, South Africa had become a democracy and women had moved into some of the country’s highest offices. Its constitution guarantees equality and protection from discrimination.

But for many women, the freedoms won through that political transformation have not translated into security, economic opportunity or reliable public services.

“How can we fully celebrate our past victories when our present reality is so deeply disappointing and distressful?” Williams-de Bruyn asked.

Her question set a sombre tone for this year’s National Women’s Day commemorations, which marked 70 years since the historic march.

What the women of 1956 won

The women who marched in 1956 were challenging one of apartheid’s most visible instruments of racial control. The pass laws regulated where Black South Africans could live and work, and the government planned to extend those restrictions to Black women.



The women delivered their petitions at the Union Buildings and stood in silence for 30 minutes before leaving. The protest became a symbol of women’s resistance and is now commemorated each year as National Women’s Day.

Nearly four decades later, apartheid was dismantled.

South Africa’s first democratic elections in 1994 brought a new political order, followed by a constitution that placed equality and human dignity at its centre. Women entered Parliament in significant numbers and moved into senior positions across government, the judiciary and other institutions.

President Cyril Ramaphosa pointed to those gains during Sunday’s commemoration, highlighting South Africa’s progress in women’s political representation, education, financial inclusion and participation in decision-making.

Women now hold some of the country’s highest positions, including chief justice, parliament speaker and public protector.

But political representation has not brought equal economic security.

“Women are more than half of our population, but they do not yet hold an equal share of our country’s wealth, its land or its enterprises,” Ramaphosa said.

Cassandra Dorasamy, a campaigner at Amnesty International South Africa, told Al Jazeera that while the country had made progress in women’s representation, it had not seen the same improvement in the lives of the majority of women.

“We’ve seen progress in terms of women’s representation in Parliament, companies and local government structures, but we have not seen the same meaningful progress in the realities of the majority of women in the country,” she said.

Violence and fear

Nowhere is that tension more visible than in South Africa’s continuing crisis of gender-based violence.

South African police recorded 9,782 reported rapes between January and March 2026, along with 12,590 sexual offences. That amounts to roughly 108 reported rapes every day.

Almost half of those reported rapes, 4,620, or 47.2 percent, took place at the home of the victim or the perpetrator, according to police statistics.

In November last year, the National Disaster Management Centre classified gender-based violence and femicide as a national disaster following sustained pressure from civil society organisations.

Ramaphosa told the gathering that women continue to live with the threat of violence “in the streets, even in their homes”.



But rights groups say declaring a disaster is only a first step.

Dorasamy said Amnesty International had heard accounts from women who struggled to open cases, were dismissed when reporting violence or received little information after making complaints.

Some women eventually withdraw their cases, she said, because the process becomes so difficult and exhausting that they no longer see a benefit in continuing.

The economic divide

The economic picture is similarly uneven.

South Africa’s unemployment rate stood at 32.7 percent in the first quarter of 2026, according to Statistics South Africa. For women, it was 36.4 percent, compared with 29.6 percent for men. Among Black African women, the unemployment rate reached 40.5 percent.

Women were also less likely than men to participate in the labour force, at 53.8 percent compared with 65.6 percent.

Among people aged 15 to 24, 39.2 percent of young women and girls were neither employed nor in education or training, compared with 36 percent of young men and boys.

For women trying to build independent lives, unemployment can deepen dependence on relatives or partners and make it harder to support children or leave abusive relationships.

In poorer and rural communities, those pressures are often compounded by limited access to land, productive resources and reliable public services.

The roots of those inequalities reach back to apartheid and earlier systems of racial dispossession, which denied Black South Africans access to land, capital and economic opportunity. Women faced additional restrictions through discriminatory laws and social structures.

Democracy changed the political system, but it did not erase decades of economic exclusion.

The unfinished promise

That tension was at the centre of Williams-de Bruyn’s speech.

She described women as prisoners in their own homes despite the democratic freedoms won after apartheid, and spoke of poverty, homelessness, a lack of clean drinking water and systemic corruption.

“We fought to dismantle the yokes of systemic oppression of women as a race, class and gender,” she said.

She received a standing ovation.

The commemorations also took on an international dimension with the attendance of Nobel Peace Prize winner Malala Yousafzai.

Ramaphosa praised Yousafzai’s courage and used the occasion to express solidarity with women and girls in Afghanistan who have been systematically excluded from education, employment and public life.

But it was Williams-de Bruyn’s reflections that lingered long after the speeches had ended.

Seventy years after that march, women hold positions of power that would have been almost unimaginable under apartheid. Yet for millions, violence, unemployment, poverty and inadequate public services still shape what freedom means in everyday life.



“This is not the freedom we marched for.”

World.title: Ceuta mayor calls for migrant detention amid mass influx crisis
World.content:
Thousands of migrants and asylum seekers in Ceuta face dire conditions, sparking political and social tensions in the Spanish territory.

Ceuta’s leader has demanded the detention and expulsion of thousands of asylum seekers and undocumented migrants roaming the streets in the Spanish North African territory after last month’s mass crossing from Morocco.

“A space that acts as an internment centre for foreigners must be set up, where these people can be held and remain confined,” Ceuta’s Mayor-President Juan Jesus Vivas of the conservative Popular Party told reporters.

He said the measure “must be achieved urgently” so that the migrants “are not in our streets and that expulsion proceedings can be handled with greater speed and ease”.

Mass border breach

A surge of asylum seekers and migrants swam or used inflatable rafts to cross from Morocco to Ceuta at the end of July, sparking a debate about the external borders of the European Union and controversy between Spain and other EU members.

Spanish authorities on Monday updated the estimated number of irregular migrants who made the journey to 80,000.

The Spanish government says 70,000 migrants and asylum seekers returned to Morocco within two days.

But the thousands who remained, including hundreds of unaccompanied children who cannot be summarily deported under Spanish law, are struggling to access food, water, shelter and sanitation, putting a strain on Ceuta’s resources.

Their future has sparked a political battle between Spain’s leftist central government and regions governed by the main conservative Popular Party and far-right Vox, which oppose taking in unaccompanied children under existing legal provisions.



Ceuta Mayor Vivas estimates that between 8,000 and 11,000 migrants are still in the Spanish territory and says the situation is “unsustainable”. He disputes the government’s statistics that only 2,500 asylum seekers and undocumented migrants remain.

Police said that 5,000 Ceuta residents gathered to protest on Sunday over the handling of the migration crisis that they say has left the enclave unsafe.

The Spanish government minister responsible for relations with the regions, Angel Victor Torres, assured Ceuta’s population that police and troop numbers had been ramped up, including 40 percent more civil guards.
