World.title: Ukraine Drone Attack on Industrial City in Russia Kills at Least 13
World.content:
A Ukrainian drone attack Monday on an industrial city about 550 miles east of Moscow was among the deadliest on Russian territory since the full-scale war began in 2022, demonstrating Kyiv’s growing ability to strike far beyond the conflict’s front lines.

At least 13 people were killed and 39 others wounded in the strikes, according to the local mayor. Russian investigators said that civilian and industrial sites had been hit in the city, Nizhnekamsk, which is home to one of Russia’s largest and most advanced oil refineries. In a statement, the country’s Investigative Committee said a child was among those killed.

Ukraine’s General Staff said that Ukrainian forces had struck the Taneko oil refinery, and that a fire had been recorded there. In recent months, Ukraine has systematically targeted Russian oil refineries to disrupt fuel supplies to the military and to civilian consumers, causing long lines at gas stations.

The Kremlin has scrambled to resolve the shortages, and lines have since dissipated in Moscow and St. Petersburg. But supply pressures remain, and oil companies now have to spend billions of dollars on repairs.

World.title: Netanyahu Walks Tightrope on Trump’s Gaza Disarmament Deal
World.content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is months away from his first national elections since the Hamas-led attack on Israel, faces an increasingly difficult challenge: how to placate President Trump, his most important ally, without alienating voters in his right-wing base.

That challenge was on full display after Mr. Trump announced last month that his Board of Peace had reached an agreement to disarm Hamas. The deal was quickly met by Israeli skepticism. Then on Sunday, Mr. Netanyahu openly rejected Mr. Trump’s plan in a rare public break with the American president.

The dispute shows how Mr. Netanyahu, who faces one of the biggest political fights of his career to win re-election in October, is being pulled in opposite directions at home and abroad.

Mr. Trump’s plan calls on Mr. Netanyahu to deliver concessions, such as pulling back Israeli troops in Gaza, which would be unpalatable to hawkish members of his constituency. At the same time, political pressure is intensifying on the prime minister as he lags behind in public opinion polls in the run-up to the election.

World.title: Police in India Use Tear Gas to Break Youth Protest
World.content:
Protesters in the eastern Indian state of Jharkhand defied police batons, tear gas, barricades and water cannons as they marched to the state legislature on Monday, demanding investigations into alleged irregularities over qualifying exams for government jobs.

Television footage showed some protesters breaking police barriers and police personnel using batons, water cannons and tear gas to disperse crowds. The scenes evoked days of protests in New Delhi, the nation’s capital in July, when thousands of demonstrators marched to Parliament to demand the resignation of India’s education minister, only to face a severe crackdown by security forces on July 20 that led to allegations of police brutality.

The march in Jharkhand, one of India’s poorest states, follows more than two weeks of protests by young people there who had demanded the cancellation of three recruitment exams for state civil services. The protesters claim that there were grading errors and financial irregularities, calling for an investigation by India’s Central Bureau of Investigation, the top federal investigative agency, and a broader overhaul of the state's recruitment system.

On Sunday, the Jharkhand government — led by the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha in alliance with the Congress and other parties — agreed to some of the students’ demands, including canceling the recruitment exams and setting up fast-track courts to speed up investigations. The head of the Jharkhand Public Services Commission and its members also resigned.

World.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
World.content:
At least 13 people have been killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on the Russian republic of Tatarstan, local officials have said.

They confirmed one child was among those killed, with 75 more people injured as drones hit Nizhnekamsk, more than 1,100 kilometres (680m) from the Ukrainian border. Ukraine's Armed Forces said the city's Tanevo oil refinery had been hit.

It is one of the deadliest single attacks on Russia since the start of Moscow's full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.

Kyiv has recently stepped up its long-range strikes on facilities it says contribute revenue and logistics to Russia's war on Ukraine.

The strike on Nizhnekamsk lasted several hours overnight and into the morning, according to local sources.

Verified images on social media show large plumes of smoke and flames rising into the sky in daytime, with air raid sirens howling in the background.

The Uzkbek consulate in Tatarstan said seven of those killed were citizens of Uzbekistan.

According to Russian news agency RIA, most of the victims had been staying in a hostel at the time of the attack, and Russia's Investigative Committee said that "civilian individuals who were not involved in any military operations were present" where the drones struck.

The BBC has not independently verified this information. Moscow said that "all those involved in the attacks" would "face inevitable and severe punishment".

Oil refineries in Nizhnekamsk had already been hit once - on 12 June.

"The facilities Ukraine targets are used to carry out attacks against Ukraine, manufacture weapons, support Russia's war effort," said Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukraine's Centre for Countering Disinformation.

World.title: Netanyahu's rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan unlikely to be final word
World.content:
In July, after months of delicate negotiations, Trump announced a "major milestone" in the implementation of his plan to end Israel's war in Gaza.

Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump said that the Board of Peace had reached an agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups in the territory.

The deal is meant to be carried out in phases, with all weapons decommissioned and stored by a new Palestinian administration in Gaza â which reports to the Board of Peace - and Israeli forces withdrawing from the more than 60% of Gaza they currently control.

Senior Hamas officials confirmed that they had agreed to the new framework, conditioning it on mutual compliance by Israel. This was widely viewed as a major potential breakthrough in the conflict. The UK welcomed it and the European Union hailed it as a "crucial step".

However, for more than a week, Israel did not give its formal response.

An Israeli spokesman said only that the roadmap did not "reflect Israel's positions." A far-right member of the government, Itamar Ben-Gvir, wrote on X that the deal was "unacceptable."

Increasingly, mainstream Israeli opposition politicians also raised doubts. They questioned whether all small arms would be decommissioned and the sequencing of the plan.

Finally on Sunday, Netanyahu told his cabinet, "I wish to be precise here: Israel does not accept the 15-point document."

He added: "The IDF [Israel Defense Forces] will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed. And when I say the disarming of Hamas, it means heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry. And we are talking about genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament."

In the same statement, the prime minister described President Trump as "the greatest of our friends in the White House" but said that Israel knew "how to stand firm" against unacceptable ideas.

In Israel, there is widespread scepticism that Hamas intends to follow through on its commitments.

The Islamist movement has long seen "armed struggle" as a core precept, its legitimate response to Israeli occupation of Palestinian lands. In recent months, there had been signs of it reasserting its authority in Gaza.

"Israel can certainly never agree to retreating anywhere where the terrorist group that caused the worst massacres since the Holocaust is still there and is still ruling the Strip," Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, an Israeli commentator and former deputy mayor of Jerusalem told the BBC.

She stressed that the "trauma of the Israeli people" from the deadly Hamas-led attacks on 7 October 2023, which ignited the devastating Gaza war, should not be underestimated.

World.title: 'We've had a lot of close calls': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
World.content:
Earl Kurz and his wife have lived in Peachland, a town overlooking Okanagan Lake in Canada's British Columbia, for 30 years. In the last 10, he said he has grown used to wildfires threatening his community.

But this is the first time he's been forced to flee, and surveying the damage left behind by the Bald Range wildfire, which broke out on Friday and grew in a matter of hours to 53 sq miles (136 sq km) in size, has been difficult.

"It's total incinerated destruction," Kurz said. "The hot spots are just barren areas of nothing except 12 inches of ash."

Officials in British Columbia are still trying to determine how many homes were lost to the fire, which remains out of control as of Monday.

World.title: Canada flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seat belt
World.content:
The cancellation of a flight in Canada after a child refused to wear a seat belt has reignited a debate about the etiquette and safety procedures relating to children travelling on planes.

The Porter Airlines flight, which was preparing to depart from Victoria to Toronto on 6 August had to return to the terminal as a "young child was standing in their seat and would not secure their seat belt", the airline said.

The delay meant the flight could not depart before the runway closed after midnight so passengers had to be rebooked on a flight the following day.

The incident has split opinion about how children should be treated in such situations and how airlines should respond.

Regarding the child's behaviour, Porter Airlines said "attempts by the accompanying parent and crew to address this were unsuccessful".

"The aircraft could not takeoff in this unsafe condition, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the two passengers disembark," it added.

Child aviation safety expert Lia Tuso told the BBC the Porter crew were protecting the safety of the passengers on the flight with their decision to stop the flight, as well as the child.

"Unrestrained children can become projectiles," Tuso said, similar to unrestrained items of luggage, which can fly into passengers in the event of turbulence, especially during takeoff and landing.

The incident has led to a debate online over how tolerant airlines should be to travelling families, and how strictly parents should enforce airline rules.

Some have said it was an example of what happens when parents are too "gentle" on their children. The Fox News morning programme debated it, with co-host Charles Hurt saying he supported physical discipline.

"We've all been those parents," he said. "But this is beyond the pale."

Other people have pointed out that sometimes children are afraid of flying and are not trying to be disruptive.

One passenger on the Porter Airlines plane, Aryeh Kozuch, told CBC News the child had not been unruly but had seemed scared.

"They just kept hiding under their seat. If they got forced into [being] strapped in, they just kind of slid out underneath."

Many have questioned why the whole flight had to be disrupted for one child and said the family should have been removed.

This is what happened in 2018, when a father and daughter were filmed being ejected from a Southwest Airlines flight from Chicago to Atlanta.

According to a passenger that filmed the incident, the child had settled down from a tantrum, and had been quietly seated in her seat for more than five minutes before the airline's crew informed the father they would be removed from the flight.

The airline involved, Southwest, said initial reports indicated "a conversation escalated onboard between the crew and a customer travelling with a small child".

After a similar incident in 2012, the family who were kicked off appeared on NBC's Today Show to accuse the airline of showing a lack of humanity.

JetBlue, the airline involved, said it "had customers that did not comply with crew member instructions for a prolonged time period".

It added: "The captain elected to remove the customers involved for the safety of all customers and crew members on board.''

With reporting from Sakshi Venkatraman

World.title: 30 years later, a former gang member will stand trial for Tupac's murder
World.content:
It's been three decades filled with mystery, conspiracies - and anger.

The drive-by shooting that killed rap superstar Tupac Shakur on 7 September 1996 changed the trajectory of hip-hop and elevated the rapper from the face of the genre to a cultural icon.

His killing became one of popular culture's great mysteries, with countless theories but no arrests until 2023, when Duane "Keffe D" Davis was unexpectedly charged with murdering the famous rapper.

The 63-year-old former gang boss is due to stand trial in Las Vegas, where he is accused of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He's pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he faces life in prison without parole.

The trial is likely to unravel the intricacies of the bitter and deadly East Coast vs West Coast rap rivalries and turf wars between the Bloods and the Crips street gangs that were immortalised in rap lyrics and news reports in the 1990s.

It could also include several celebrity witnesses - including Suge Knight, the former CEO of Death Row Records, who has been thought of as the last surviving witness to Shakur's death.

But the complicated case hinges almost exclusively on one key piece of evidence: a book co-authored by Davis that he has argued is partially a piece of fiction.

Jury selection in the case began on Monday, with opening arguments due to start on 17 August.

World.title: We are chasing Ebola virus - it is ahead of us, WHO warns
World.content:
The latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo began at least three months before it was officially declared - meaning the health authorities are still playing catch-up, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

More than 1,900 people have died from the virus since that declaration on 15 May, making this the second-worst Ebola outbreak ever.

Infection rates are still high, adding to the concern that the authorities are struggling to get to grips with the spread of the disease.

The epicentre of this outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, is in the east of DR Congo where insecurity has hampered control efforts.

There is also no approved vaccine or any recognised therapeutic drugs, making treating Bundibugyo harder.

"We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us," WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said at a news conference in the city of Bunia, which is at the heart of this outbreak.

He cited research showing that the virus started spreading in February and was initially misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid.

Janabi also said that, in part because of insecurity, health workers are only reaching about 30% of the cases with the rest dying at home.

Traditional burial practices â where mourners touch the deceased's body - and a suspicion of health authorities in some communities have also made things difficult.

But there are now several dedicated treatment centres in the east of DR Congo and people are getting diagnosed much more quickly.

So far there have been 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths, DR Congo's health ministry has said.

The largest recorded outbreak was in West Africa between 2014 and 2016 when 11,325 people died.

World.title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
World.content:
President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) shots.

"Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today," Trump said on Monday. "In those times, people were much healthier and of course the high rates of autism now observed did not exist."

The president has long cast doubt on the safety of MMR vaccines, but multiple studies have found no connection between the shots and autism.

The order also recommends that the number of childhood vaccines drop to 11 from the existing 18 recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump said that his administration "is recognising gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases".

The immunisations recommended for all children under the order are for measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and varicella or chicken pox.

"We're reducing them," Trump said. "It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor."

The president suggested that the MMR vaccine could be "quite lethal" if given at once. He compared it to pouring a bottle of soda into a child's body.

Experts say that allowing time between jabs means children are more likely to contract diseases in the interim or that they are more likely to miss appointments if there are multiple shots.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, external (CDC), there is "no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots".

The agency says "most people who get MMR vaccine do not have any serious problems with it", and that getting the vaccine "is much safer than getting measles, mumps, or rubella".

Trump's Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F Kennedy Jr said the proposed changes were meant to give parents choice, not prohibit access to childhood vaccines.

The federal government does not have the authority to implement the new recommendations. Shots that are required for school attendance are set at the state level.

Dr Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, called Trump's executive order "disheartening" and "dangerous", pointing out it comes as measles cases reach a 35-year high in the US. Measles cases have also been rising globally.

"Instead of ensuring every family can access life-saving vaccines for measles, influenza, RSV and more, federal leaders are once again spreading misleading claims," Racine said in a statement on Monday.

He said there was no new evidence to justify the significant changes, adding that the order was not based on "gold-standard science".

"Delaying or skipping shots is risky, especially as measles continues to spread and children go back to school," Racine said.

Republican Senator Bill Cassidy also admonished Trump's executive order on Monday, labelling it "wrong".

"The President does not have the expertise to make these changes," Cassidy, who is a physician, wrote on social media. "Vaccines are overwhelmingly safe. Vaccines are effective. Vaccines DO NOT cause autism."

The lawmaker, who chairs the Senate health committee, urged parents to "listen to their child's pediatrician about vaccines rather than listening to an inaccurate executive order".

Experts fear that if parents refrain from getting their children vaccinated as a result of the discredited idea that childhood vaccines are linked to autism, it risks the re-emergence of diseases like measles.

Multiple studies have found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism. A recent high-quality study from Denmark in 2019 looked at 657,461 children and concluded that the data did not support the MMR vaccine causing or triggering autism.

On its website, the US CDC recommends that two doses of the combined MMR vaccine be given to children, starting with the first dose at 12-15 months and the second between the ages of four and six.

How often and how many vaccines children in the US receive is based on the times when vaccines will work best with their immune systems and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases, according to the AAP.

There is no medical reason to delay or skip recommended immunisations, the AAP says.

World.title: World's oceans hit record-high July temperatures
World.content:
The world's oceans hit their hottest ever recorded temperatures for July, partly fuelled by developing El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific, according to the EU's climate monitoring service.

The average sea surface temperature (SST) outside the world's polar regions - between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south - was 20.96C last month, beating the previous high of 20.89C, set in 2023.

Last month was the joint second-warmest July globally on record, with temperatures 1.47C above the estimated pre-industrial average, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

Meanwhile, Western Europe experienced its hottest ever June and July, with prolonged hot and dry conditions fuelling extreme wildfires across the region.

Elsewhere, the UK is braced for its fifth heatwave of the year this week, as persistent dry weather puts further pressure on water supplies and could see more areas officially declared in drought.

World.title: Heirs Life Assurance appoints Pastor Jerry Eze as Non-Executive Director
World.content:
Heirs Life Assurance, the specialist life insurance company of Heirs Insurance Group, has appointed Pastor Jerry Eze as an Independent Non-Executive Director on its Board, effective 10 August 2026.

The appointment reinforces Heirs Life Assurance’s commitment to expanding financial inclusion and accelerating insurance adoption by strengthening public trust, consumer education, and long-term financial resilience across Nigeria.

Despite being Africa’s largest economy, Nigeria’s insurance penetration remains below one percent – among the lowest globally – highlighting the need to expand financial protection and build greater public trust in insurance. As Heirs Life continues to pursue its mission of making insurance accessible to every Nigerian, Eze’s appointment brings a unique perspective on community engagement, value-based leadership, and broad societal impact.

Pastor Jerry Eze is the Founder and Lead Pastor of Streams of Joy International Ministry, a growing multinational ministry with 34 branches across West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe and North America. He is also the convener of the New Season Prophetic Prayers and Declaration (NSPPD), one of the world’s largest digital prayer platforms, reaching millions of people daily. Through his ministry and humanitarian initiatives, he has become one of Africa’s most influential voices, championing hope, compassion, and community transformation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond ministry, Eze is the Founder of the Jerry Eze Foundation, a faith-led philanthropy where he provides housing support and grants to vulnerable and underserved communities. In 2026, he announced N1billion in grants to support young entrepreneurs across agriculture, technology, and manufacturing, further advancing enterprise development and economic opportunity.

Before entering full-time ministry, Pastor Jerry Eze built a career in development communications, serving as a Communications Specialist on a World Bank HIV/AIDS programme and with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

He holds a Bachelor’s degree in History and International Relations from Abia State University and a postgraduate degree in Business Administration from Enugu State University of Science and Technology.

Speaking about the appointment, Tony O Elumelu, Chairman, Heirs Life Assurance, said:

“Pastor Jerry brings an exceptional combination of integrity, influence, and a deep understanding of people and communities. As we continue our mission to democratise access to insurance, his insight will help strengthen consumer trust, deepen financial inclusion, and reinforce our commitment to protecting the financial future of millions of Nigerians. We are delighted to welcome him to the Board of Heirs Life Assurance and the broader family of Heirs Insurance Group.”

Commenting on his appointment, Pastor Jerry Eze said:

“I am honoured to join the Board of Heirs Life Assurance at a defining moment for the insurance industry. Financial security empowers individuals, families, and businesses to pursue their aspirations with greater confidence and resilience.

“I look forward to working with the Board and Management to advance the company’s mission of making insurance more accessible, relevant, and impactful for every Nigerian”.

Heirs Life Assurance has become one of Nigeria’s leading specialist life insurance companies, ranking 7th on the Financial Times list of Africa’s fastest-growing companies. It is one of the three insurance businesses of Heirs Holdings, the leading pan-African investment company, with investments across 24 countries and four continents.

Combining an omni-channel digital presence with physical branches spread across the country, Heirs Life continues to redefine life insurance through innovation, customer-centric solutions, and a commitment to making financial protection accessible to every Nigerian.

Heirs Insurance Group, comprising Heirs Life Assurance, Heirs General Insurance, and Heirs Insurance Brokers, collectively serves over 3 million people directly and indirectly. The Group is championing financial inclusion and leading the digital insurance play in Nigeria, demonstrating its mission to democratise access to insurance.

World.title: Delta govt suspends works commissioner, gives reasons
World.content:
The Delta State Government on Monday suspended the State Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads) Reuben Izeze, for allegedly assaulting his aide, Simon Mudi.

The suspension notice is contained in a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Kingsley Emu in Asaba.

The suspension is linked to a viral video of a fracas at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in July during a Delta Central Stakeholders meeting of the All Progressives Congress.

Although the fracas did not take place in the APC meeting hall, the governor’s aide was assaulted on the premises after the meeting, prompting Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to order an investigation into the matter.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

As earlier reported by PREMIUM TIMES, the video shows participants fleeing in panic as several men pursued Mr Mudi, also known as “Temple,” striking him on the head with bottles and throwing chairs at him while he attempted to escape.

Mr Mudi was later seen in the clip dressed in an APC-branded safari receiving treatment in a hospital with visible bruises and a bloodied head.

Although the immediate cause of the attack could not be independently established, the violence underscored growing concerns that political tensions could escalate as parties begin positioning for the 2027 elections.

Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, who recently defected from the APC to the National Democratic Congress (NDC), said the incident reflected an emerging pattern of political violence in Delta.

In a statement issued by his spokesman, Godwin Anaughe, Mr Omo-Agege described the assault as “political thuggery”.

“A meeting of leaders from a registered political party was violently broken up, and a serving government official was assaulted with dangerous weapons in broad daylight. That this could happen at all says something deeply troubling about where Delta State’s politics is headed,” he said.

Mr Omo-Agege alleged, without presenting evidence, that the attackers were sponsored. He also linked the incident to an earlier alleged attack on NDC governorship candidate in the state, Chris Iyovwaye, who he claimed was prevented by hoodlums from entering his hometown of Agholokpe.

Claiming both incidents were connected, he alleged that the APC was preparing “a coordinated campaign of violence and intimidation” ahead of the 2027 elections to suppress opposition strongholds.

The former deputy Senate president called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Commissioner of Police in Delta and the State Security Service to investigate the incidents, prosecute those responsible and ensure a peaceful political environment before the next general election.

The Delta State Government had rejected the allegations, insisting that the incident should not be exploited for political purposes.

READ ALSO: Ten oil spills recorded in Niger Delta in July

Why Delta govt suspended commissioner – SSG

The SSG, Mr Emu said the decision to suspend the works commissioner was taken to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into the incident.

He said the state administration remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and to protecting the sanctity of human life.

According to the SSG, these principles will be upheld even when state institutions are involved.

He said the suspension is indefinite, pending the outcome of the investigation.

(NAN)

World.title: FCMB, stakeholders set out roadmap to move Nigeria’s health sector from survival to scale
World.content:
Nigeria’s healthcare sector needs more than additional funding to expand. It needs businesses capable of attracting capital, deploying it effectively and building institutions that can grow sustainably, healthcare stakeholders have said.

That challenge was at the centre of the inaugural First City Monument Bank (FCMB) Healthcare Summit in Lagos, where the bank unveiled a N20 billion Healthcare Fund to support private healthcare businesses.

The fund will provide financing to hospitals, clinics, diagnostic centres, pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies, maternity homes and other businesses across the healthcare value chain.

The summit, themed “Financing Growth: Unlocking Opportunity, Building the Future of Healthcare,” brought together policymakers, healthcare providers, investors, financial institutions and development partners to examine how more private capital can be channelled into Nigeria’s health sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At the heart of the discussions was a persistent financing problem: healthcare providers struggle to access affordable, long-term capital, while lenders and investors often require stronger governance, financial reporting and business structures before committing funds.

“Healthcare is a social imperative and an economic priority,” FCMB Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Yemisi Edun said in remarks delivered by Executive Director, Corporate Services and Service Management Felicia Obozuwa. “Building a strong healthcare system requires patient, affordable and long-term capital.”

Mrs Edun said financing alone would not be sufficient. Healthcare businesses also need sound governance, capable leadership and strategic partnerships to build resilient institutions.

Through the new fund, FCMB plans to finance infrastructure expansion, medical equipment, working capital, technology adoption and other investments aimed at improving efficiency and service delivery.

The push for more private capital comes as the government increases public investment in healthcare and seeks to expand capacity across the sector.

Government investment

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, said more than N339 billion has been disbursed through the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund over the past 12 years.

Of that amount, N235 billion was disbursed in the last three years under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, he said.

Mr Salako added that another N32.9 billion was recently disbursed to support more than 8,300 primary healthcare centres, while the government is targeting about 13,000 facilities nationwide.

Beyond healthcare facilities, the government is seeking to increase domestic production of medicines and medical equipment.

Under the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain, Nigeria is targeting local production of 70 per cent of medicines and medical devices by 2030.

Mr Salako also highlighted initiatives aimed at addressing electricity constraints in healthcare facilities and creating long-term procurement opportunities for local manufacturers.

Making healthcare businesses bankable

For private healthcare operators, however, access to affordable capital remains a major obstacle to expansion.

The President of the Healthcare Federation of Nigeria (HFN), Njide Ndili, said affordable, long-term financing is one of the biggest barriers facing private healthcare businesses.

She said experience from HFN’s partnership with the PharmAccess Medical Credit Fund demonstrated that healthcare small and medium-sized enterprises could become bankable when financing is combined with technical support, capacity building and quality standards.

The challenge, therefore, is not simply increasing the amount of money available to healthcare providers but ensuring that businesses are prepared to attract and manage investment.

HFN will work with FCMB to develop a framework for pre-qualifying eligible healthcare facilities and helping businesses become investment-ready.

The federation, which has more than 400 member organisations and 4,000 professionals, will support businesses in strengthening governance, financial reporting, management capacity and growth plans before accessing financing.

From survival to scale

Discussions at the summit examined how healthcare operators can move beyond managing day-to-day pressures and build institutions capable of attracting long-term investment.

Participants explored blended finance, alternative lending structures and public-private partnerships as possible mechanisms for attracting more domestic and international capital.

An executive discussion on building healthcare businesses that attract investment also highlighted the importance of sound business management, governance, risk management and clear growth strategies alongside clinical performance.

Four broad priorities emerged from the discussions: expanding access to fit-for-purpose capital, improving the bankability of healthcare businesses, strengthening public-private partnerships and increasing domestic capacity in pharmaceuticals, diagnostics and medical equipment.

FCMB’s N20 billion fund is positioned within that broader agenda, complementing government investment with private financing for businesses seeking to expand facilities, purchase equipment, adopt technology and improve service delivery.

The summit was organised in partnership with the Health Business Academy for Africa.

For stakeholders, the next challenge is translating the financing commitments and partnerships announced at the summit into stronger healthcare businesses and increased capacity across the sector.

The broader goal is to create a healthcare ecosystem in which stronger institutions, sustainable financing and strategic partnerships translate into greater access to quality healthcare for Nigerians.

World.title: Ten oil spills recorded in Niger Delta in July
World.content:
At least 10 oil spill incidents were recorded across Rivers, Delta, Bayelsa and Imo states in July, according to a PREMIUM TIMES review of the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA)’s Oil Spill Monitor.

The incidents involved major oil producers, including Renaissance Africa Energy Company, Heirs Energies, Seplat Energy, Oando and Sterling Oil Exploration and Energy Production Company (SEEPCO), with sabotage, corrosion, operational failures and equipment defects identified as the leading causes.

The review shows that Rivers State accounted for the highest number of reported incidents during the month, while pipeline infrastructure remained the most affected oil facility.

The spills occurred despite successive federal administrations committing billions of naira annually to pipeline surveillance and protection contracts aimed at reducing crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism and associated environmental pollution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES has previously reported that although the federal government continues to increase spending on pipeline protection, oil-producing communities remain vulnerable to recurring spills, while clean-up and remediation efforts often lag behind.

The newspaper has also consistently reported concerns by environmental experts and civil society organisations that greater emphasis should be placed on preventing oil spills through improved pipeline integrity, maintenance and regulatory enforcement rather than relying largely on surveillance contracts.

Rivers records most incidents

NOSDRA records show that Renaissance Africa Energy Company recorded four separate spill incidents during the month.

The largest was reported on 16 July in Burutu Local Government Area of Delta State, where 25 barrels of crude oil, equivalent to about 3,980 litres, escaped from a pipeline due to operational and maintenance error.

The spill affected swamp vegetation, surface water and fishing nets both within and outside the company’s right of way.

NOSDRA directed the company to repair the damaged section of the pipeline, recover free-phase crude oil and undertake clean-up under the agency’s supervision.

On the same day, another Renaissance incident occurred in Oguta Local Government Area of Imo State, where 0.1 barrels (about 16 litres) of crude oil spilled following sabotage and oil theft, affecting surrounding vegetation.

The company also reported a four-barrel spill on 8 July at Elele Alimini in Emohua West Local Government Area of Rivers State.

According to the Joint Investigation Visit (JIV) report, the spill resulted from sabotage and theft and impacted vegetation, including palm trees that had encroached on the pipeline right of way.

A fourth Renaissance incident, reported on 4 July in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers, initially indicated a spill on land.

However, the JIV later concluded it was a false alarm after excavation found no leak on the pipeline.

Corrosion, sabotage persist

The review also identified corrosion as a recurring cause of spills.

On 27 July, SEEPCO recorded a spill of 10 barrels, or about 1,590 litres, of crude oil in Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area of Imo State.

The spill, reportedly caused by corrosion, was contained two days later.

Similarly, Oando reported a one-barrel spill caused by pipeline corrosion on 5 July in Okoroma, Nembe Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Earlier, on 3 July, Oando reported another incident involving nine barrels of condensate at Otua community in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers.

Investigators found a 0.5-millimetre drill hole on the facility’s flowline, indicating a sabotage.

Operational failures

Operational and equipment failures also contributed to pollution during the month.

Aiteo Exploration and Production Company recorded a spill of 17 barrels, approximately 2,700 litres, on 13 July at its Central Processing Facility connected to the Nembe Crude Oil Export Terminal in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

NOSDRA attributed the incident to an overflow within the facility’s storage system.

On 11 July, Seplat Energy recorded a spill of 0.5 barrels, about 80 litres, in Okpe Local Government Area of Delta State following equipment failure.

The spill affected seasonal swamp surface water.

NOSDRA recommended immediate repairs to the damaged equipment and prompt removal of oil sheen from the affected water body.

Sabotage blamed for Heirs Energies spill

On 28 July, Heirs Energies reported a spill from the Nkale Well 13 Flowline in Odogwa I, Etche Local Government Area of Rivers.

NOSDRA assigned the incident number IN-0855 and estimated the volume at 0.0126 barrels, equivalent to about two litres of crude oil.

The spill stopped on 31 July and the JIV attributed the incident to sabotage.

Environmental concerns remain

The July incidents add to the long list of oil spills recorded annually across the Niger Delta, where repeated pollution has devastated farmlands, rivers, wetlands and fishing communities.

PREMIUM TIMES has, in several investigations, documented how delayed clean-up, ageing infrastructure, weak regulatory enforcement and persistent pipeline vandalism continue to undermine efforts to reduce environmental pollution in the region.

The newspaper has also reported calls by environmental groups for oil companies and regulators to prioritise pipeline replacement, stronger maintenance regimes, faster remediation and stricter accountability to reduce the frequency of spills and protect livelihoods in oil-producing communities.

World.title: Nigerian Law School confirms student’s death at Lagos Campus
World.content:
The Nigerian Law School has confirmed the death of a student who fell from the rooftop of a hostel at its Lagos Campus.

The student, who was from the Enugu Campus, was in Lagos for the school’s externship programme and was temporarily accommodated at the Lagos Campus hostel.

The school, in a statement shared on its Facebook on Monday by the Secretary to the Council and Director of Administration, Aderonke Osho, said the incident occurred at about 4 a.m. on Friday, 7 August.

“Preliminary information indicates that, at about 4:00am on Friday, 7 August 2026, the student fell from the rooftop of the hostel at the Campus and, sadly, succumbed to the incident,” the statement stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The school did not name the student or disclose what led to the fall.

It noted that it was working with the relevant authorities and the deceased student’s family to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

“The Management is working closely with the appropriate authorities and the family to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, ensure that all necessary procedures are duly followed, and provide further information as appropriate,” Mr Osho said.

The management expressed condolences to the student’s family, colleagues and others affected by the death.

It also appealed to the public and the media to respect the family’s request for privacy as they mourned.

The school said the family had asked that they be allowed to grieve without actions that could further compound their pain.

The Nigerian Law School added that it remained committed to the safety, welfare and wellbeing of its students and staff.

Police reported suspected suicide

The school’s confirmation followed an earlier report on Sunday that the deceased was 23-year-old Faith Alayande and that the Lagos State Police Command had confirmed the incident.

According to the report, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abimbola Adebisi, said the incident was reported after the student was found unresponsive within the hostel premises.

Ms Adebisi reportedly stated that a hostel matron alerted the police and that a fellow student and a relative had found what was described as a suicide note.

She was quoted as saying the student allegedly jumped from the rooftop of the four-storey hostel building before she could be located.

The report said the student’s body was later taken to a morgue, while the police commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death.

READ ALSO: University suspends law students over examination malpractices

However, while the police account reported by PUNCH, suggested a suspected suicide, the Nigerian Law School’s Monday statement described the incident simply as a fall from the hostel rooftop and did not state that the student died by suicide.

The latest incident is not the first reported death of a Nigerian Law School student in circumstances linked to suicide.

In December 2025, another student, Ayomiposi Ojajuni, allegedly died by suicide after he was reportedly barred from sitting for the Bar Final examinations at the school’s Yola Campus in Adamawa State.

World.title: Enugu targets 20-hour power supply with 3 new project
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has commenced the construction of three new 33KV feeders to provide improved, affordable, and stable electricity supply to communities in four local government areas of the state.

The project, which is being developed from the Ugwuaji Transmission Station, will serve communities in Nkanu East, Nkanu West, Aninri, and Awgu council areas.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the inauguration of the project was preceded by a stakeholders’ meeting on electricity held at the International Conference Centre, Enugu, on Saturday.

Speaking at the event, Christopher Ezeoha, managing director and CEO of the Enugu State Electrification Agency (ESEA) said the project aimed at addressing the longstanding electricity challenges in the affected communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ezeoha said Nkanu East and Nkanu West have been grossly underserved because a single feeder currently supplies a very large area.

He explained that the Amechi 33KV feeder serves eight council areas—five in Enugu State and three in Ebonyi State—covering a distance of more than 640 kilometres.

According to him, the length of the feeder makes it difficult to identify and resolve faults whenever they occur, resulting in prolonged power outages.

“Some communities, including Nkerifi, Nara, and Mburubu, have not had electricity for more than 20 years,” he said.

Mr Ezeoha said the state government had directed the agency to restore electricity to such communities but noted that simply restoring the existing feeder would not solve the problem.

He said: “Government has therefore decided to break the long feeder into shorter sections by constructing about three new feeders of roughly 200 kilometres or less each.

“Injection substations will also be installed to transform electricity from 33KV to 11KV, thereby improving the reliability of supply to communities.

“By the time we finish this work, we hope to give them an average of more than 20 hours of daily power supply. That’s what the government has directed us to do.”

Mr Ezeoha said the initiative would not be limited to the four local government area, adding that similar interventions would be extended to other parts of the state, including Nsukka and Uzo-Uwani.

He said the state government was also preparing its electricity distribution infrastructure to evacuate power from a proposed 630-megawatt generation facility being developed in the state.

According to him, the state government’s long-term objective is to provide reliable electricity supply for 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

Mr Ezeoha said the government also planned to deploy smart prepaid meters and automation technology to improve accountability and enable quick detection and resolution of faults.

He said a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system would enable the agency to know the location of faults almost immediately, allowing technical personnel to respond directly to the affected point instead of searching along hundreds of kilometres of transmission lines.

The ESEA boss appealed to communities to protect electrical infrastructure against vandalism, stressing that the success of the investment depended on collective ownership and protection of the facilities.

Concern over vandalism of transmission infrastructure

Also speaking, Tom Inugonum, general manager of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), Enugu, commended the state government for its efforts to improve electricity supply.

Mr Inugonum said the TCN Enugu region controls transmission infrastructure covering between six and eight states, adding that improved cooperation with the Enugu State Government would help address the state’s power challenges.

He said Enugu receives electricity from three major sources and had several transmission lines serving different parts of the state.

According to him, some transmission and substation projects in the region remain incomplete, limiting the capacity of the power system.

He expressed concern over the vandalism of transmission infrastructure, citing the value of substations and other facilities that could be lost if they were not adequately protected.

Also speaking, Enyinna Ogbonna, the commissioner for energy in Enugu, said electricity was one of the major priorities of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration.

READ ALSO: Suspected thief dies while allegedly vandalising TCN electricity transmission tower

Mr Ogbonna said reliable electricity was critical to driving the state’s economy and achieving the administration’s target of increasing Enugu’s Gross Domestic Product from about $4.4 billion to $30 billion.

In his remarks, Okey Nwatu, President-General of Isi-Amagunze, called for greater community involvement in protecting electricity infrastructure.

Mr Nwatu said transformers, cables, switches, and other electrical facilities were critical infrastructure that communities must protect if they want to enjoy sustained electricity supply.

(NAN)

World.title: University suspends law students over examination malpractices
World.content:
The Management of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) has suspended three undergraduates of the Faculty of Law for two academic years over examination malpractice.

The suspension, which took effect from 25 June 2026, will run until 24 June 2028.

This is contained in separate memos addressed to the affected students by the university’s Registrar, Ambrose Ugwu, on Monday in Enugu, and made available to reporters.

The affected students, comprising two males and one female, are Isong Ugwu, with registration No. ESUT/2023030212973; Gad Nwosu, registration No. ESUT/2022030203441; and Roseline Nnamani, registration No. ESUT/2024030219772.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ugwu said the Vice-Chancellor of the university, Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, acting on behalf of the University Senate, approved the recommendations of the Senate Examinations Malpractice Committee.

The registrar directed the affected students to hand over any university property in their possession to their respective Heads of Department and vacate the university campus immediately.

He added that the sponsors of the affected students and the National Universities Commission had been informed of the development.

According to him, the students will be required to apply for readmission upon the expiration of their suspension in June 2028.

READ ALSO: Tinubu appoints first female DG of Nigerian Law School

Meanwhile, another student of the Faculty of Law, Goodluck Iwuamadi, with registration No. ESUT/2025030227502, was exonerated from an allegation of examination malpractice.

Mr Ugwu said the decision to exonerate Mr Iwuamadi was in line with the recommendation of the Senate Examinations Malpractice Committee.

World.title: NDLEA, army seize 604.5kg cannabis, hunt suspected drug kingpin
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in collaboration with the Nigerian Army, has seized 604.5kg of cannabis and launched a manhunt for a suspected drug kingpin in Owan West Local Government Area of Edo State.

The State Commander of NDLEA, Mitchell Ofoyeju, disclosed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria on Monday in Benin.

Mr Ofoyeju said the operation was conducted on 5 August at Ewe Luleha, a suspected drug hub in Owan West, where operatives recovered 65 bags of dried weeds that tested positive for skunk cannabis.

He said the command launched a manhunt for the suspected kingpin identified only as Sunday, who reportedly fled during the operation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are tracking the suspected drug kingpin, one Sunday, who is in hiding, following recovery of the 604.5kg of cannabis.

“He has nowhere to hide because we will certainly apprehend him,” Mr Ofoyeju said.

The commander said the operation formed part of the agency’s renewed efforts to dismantle drug trafficking networks across Edo.

He said nine suspected drug peddlers were also arrested in separate operations conducted at various drug hotspots in the state.

Mr Ofoyeju said the suspects comprised five males and four females.

According to him, the suspects were arrested with varying quantities of cannabis, loud, colorado, methamphetamine and tramadol.

He said the arrests and seizures demonstrated the command’s continued efforts to disrupt the supply and distribution of illicit drugs in Edo.

The NDLEA commander urged residents to support the agency by providing credible information that could assist in apprehending fleeing suspects and dismantling drug trafficking networks.

“These arrests and drug seizures not only highlight law enforcement efforts but also signify the increasing need for community involvement in reporting illicit activities.

“I urge members of the public to provide any information that may lead to the apprehension of the fleeing suspects and to support ongoing efforts to combat drug abuse and trafficking in Edo State,” he said.

Mr Ofoyeju assured that investigations into the drug-related activities would continue and that suspects would be prosecuted in accordance with the law.
